elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT using the exact module name `i2c_master_bit_ctrl`, with its declared clock, reset, command, bus, status, and data ports connected in a minimal testbench.
elements.expected_response: Compilation and elaboration succeed, and the instantiated `i2c_master_bit_ctrl` is available as the bit-level controller DUT without missing, extra, or direction-incompatible required ports.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator/compiler elaboration result and an interface-signature assertion or compile-time port binding check; record a passing bin only when the exact module instance elaborates successfully.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold filtered SCL and SDA high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue cmd=START (4'b0001) on a timing-enable opportunity, then maintain ena=1 and the released-high bus until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: the supported command is translated into a timed open-drain sequence. scl_oen and sda_oen leave the idle released state and transition at the command phase boundaries: SDA is driven low while SCL remains released, then SCL is driven low, and both outputs return to the appropriate released/complete state with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked reference model of command acceptance and START phases; sample scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge, verify the expected ordered released/low-enable transitions and completion, and assert that no phase transition occurs without the modeled timing-enable tick.

elements.stimulus: After reset while the controller is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1, issue unsupported cmd=4'b0011 for multiple enabled clock opportunities, and keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of shows: scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the idle released state throughout; no timed SCL/SDA command sequence occurs and cmd_ack is never asserted.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen on every posedge against the idle-release values (both 1), monitor the complete stimulus window for any driven-low enable or phase transition, and assert cmd_ack remains 0.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt to a nonzero value, hold scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=START on an enabled command-processing tick, and keep the external bus released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module generates a START waveform by releasing SCL, driving SDA low while SCL is high, then driving SCL low; cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock at command completion, and busy becomes asserted when the filtered START is detected.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the enabled FSM phases and sample registered outputs after each posedge; assert the required sda_oen/scl_oen ordering, one-cycle cmd_ack, and busy assertion after the filtered SDA falling transition.

elements.stimulus: After a busy transaction, set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP on an enabled tick while the external bus is initially high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module drives SDA low, releases SCL and waits for filtered SCL high, then releases SDA while SCL is high; cmd_ack pulses once and busy clears when the filtered STOP is detected.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed sda_oen/scl_oen sequence and registered status outputs against a STOP reference model, allowing variable prescaler and synchronization latency.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue cmd=WRITE twice, first with din=0 and then with din=1; allow each command to complete with SCL rising and falling normally.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: for din=0 the module drives SDA low during the bit; for din=1 it releases SDA. Each command releases SCL for the high phase, pulls it low for completion, produces one cmd_ack pulse, and does not assert al when the observed SDA matches the driven value.
elements.check_method: Check each registered open-drain enable against din and the modeled WRITE phase sequence; verify command completion and al=0 with a cycle-accurate reference model.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE with ena=1 and din=1; during the released SCL-high phase force the external SDA line low, then release both external lines.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because released-high SDA is observed low, arbitration is lost; al asserts and remains asserted, the active command aborts, cmd_ack does not pulse, and both scl_oen and sda_oen become released.
elements.check_method: Inject the bus value through an open-drain model, detect the filtered SDA-low arbitration condition during the WRITE high phase, and compare al, cmd_ack, FSM completion, and output enables with the arbitration-loss reference model.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released bus, issue cmd=READ; provide SDA=0 for one trial and SDA=1 for another, and provide a normal filtered SCL rising edge followed by SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module releases SDA, releases SCL for the read window, captures the filtered SDA value into dout exactly at the filtered SCL rising edge, pulls SCL low, and produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Drive the external bus with an open-drain model and compare dout capture edge, sda_oen/scl_oen phases, and cmd_ack against the READ reference model for both data values.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=READ with ena=1, release SCL from the DUT, and hold the external SCL line low for several enabled timing ticks before allowing it to rise.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module remains in the SCL-high/read waiting phase while filtered SCL is low; the timing counter and FSM do not advance, then the read phase resumes after filtered SCL becomes high, captures dout on the filtered rising edge, and eventually acknowledges.
elements.check_method: Monitor the slave-wait behavior and compare phase transitions and completion time with a reference model that pauses the counter and FSM during clock stretching.

elements.stimulus: During a command phase in which the DUT has released SCL, drive an external SCL falling transition while the DUT expects SCL high, then restore the bus and continue the command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the module recognizes multi-master clock synchronization from the filtered external SCL falling edge, reloads its timing counter, and does not advance the high-phase timing as though SCL had remained high; the command later completes with its normal acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed delay and subsequent phase ordering against a reference model containing filtered SCL edge detection and timing-counter reload; verify no false al or premature cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Run an enabled START, WRITE, READ, and STOP sequence with clk_cnt values 0, 1, and a larger value, while keeping the external bus valid for each command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: every supported command produces its required waveform and exactly one completion pulse for all prescaler values; clk_cnt=0 does not stall the divider, and larger values only increase the modeled timing intervals.
elements.check_method: Use a divider/filter reference model for each clk_cnt value and assert phase ordering, eventual completion, one-cycle cmd_ack, and absence of stuck timing behavior.

elements.stimulus: While idle with ena=1, apply raw SDA/SCL pulses shorter than the filter sampling interval, including a short SDA high-to-low pulse while SCL is high and a short SDA low-to-high pulse while SCL is high; do not issue a command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because the glitches do not change the majority-filtered inputs, no START or STOP is detected, busy does not change, al remains deasserted, and no command waveform or cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Model the two-stage synchronizers, sample interval, three-sample histories, and majority filter; assert that filtered transitions and all associated registered outputs remain unchanged.

elements.stimulus: While idle with ena=1, apply stable SDA and SCL transitions that persist through multiple filter samples: first SDA high-to-low while SCL is high, then SDA low-to-high while SCL is high; repeat with transitions applied asynchronously between clk edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: synchronized and filtered transitions are eventually recognized despite asynchronous input timing; busy rises for the filtered START and clears for the filtered STOP, with status changes occurring only after the corresponding filtered transitions rather than at raw input edges.
elements.check_method: Compare output status timing and filtered transition events against a synchronization/filter reference model, allowing the modeled synchronizer and filter latency.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus released high, issue each supported command encoding on an enabled tick, then issue NOP and unsupported command values while idle.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for supported commands: START, STOP, WRITE, and READ select their corresponding waveform, complete, and pulse cmd_ack once. Contrasting case for NOP and unsupported values: the FSM remains idle, both lines remain released, and cmd_ack does not pulse.
elements.check_method: Decode command values in the reference model and compare command-specific sda_oen/scl_oen traces, idle behavior, and cmd_ack pulses after each stimulus.

elements.stimulus: Start an enabled WRITE or READ command, then force an unexpected filtered STOP by driving SDA from low to high while filtered SCL is high; separately run the same command without the unexpected STOP.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: an unexpected STOP during an active non-STOP command asserts sticky al, aborts the command, releases both output enables, and suppresses cmd_ack. Holding case: without the unexpected STOP, the command completes normally with al deasserted and one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use filtered bus transitions to trigger the error in one trial and a normal bus trace in the other; compare sticky al, abort behavior, line release, and command acknowledgement with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and clk_cnt set to a small nonzero value; provide a released-high external bus and run until the START sequence reaches its phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: For the SCL drive-low case in observed_via.shows, scl_o remains 0 and scl_oen becomes 0, so the open-drain SCL control drives the line low. sda_o also remains 0; SDA control may be observed according to the START phase.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through the SCL-low phase, assert scl_o==0 and, when the SCL drive phase is active, scl_oen==0; with the external SCL driver released, check the modeled SCL line is low. Record a bin for the active-low SCL drive case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and a released-high external bus; observe the initial START phase before the controller pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting SCL release case in observed_via.shows, scl_o remains 0 and scl_oen is 1, selecting release rather than drive. With no external low drive, the modeled SCL line remains high.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_o and scl_oen after each registered update during the initial START phase; assert scl_o==0, scl_oen==1, and the open-drain bus model resolves SCL high. Record a bin for the SCL release case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and a released-high external bus; run through the phase in which START pulls SDA low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: For the SDA drive-low case in observed_via.shows, sda_o remains 0 and sda_oen becomes 0, selecting drive-low for SDA. The modeled SDA line is low while SCL remains released and high.
elements.check_method: At settled posedges covering the START SDA-low phase, assert sda_o==0 and sda_oen==0; resolve the modeled open-drain SDA line with the external driver released and compare it with low. Record a bin for the active-low SDA drive case.

elements.stimulus: After completing a busy transaction, issue a STOP command with ena high; run until the STOP sequence releases SDA after SCL has been released high.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting SDA release case in observed_via.shows, sda_o remains 0 and sda_oen is 1, selecting release rather than drive. With no external low drive, the modeled SDA line rises high while SCL is high.
elements.check_method: After the registered STOP release update, assert sda_o==0 and sda_oen==1, and check the open-drain bus model resolves SDA high with the external driver released. Record a bin for the SDA release case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and clk_cnt set to a small nonzero value. Allow the START sequence to reach its phases, including SDA driven low while SCL is high and then SCL driven low.
elements.expected_response: Drive-side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain 0 at all observed times; during each phase that drives SCL or SDA low, the corresponding output-enable is 0 (scl_oen=0 for SCL drive and sda_oen=0 for SDA drive), and the observed bus line is low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge from command acceptance through completion, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and compare each output-enable and modeled open-drain bus line against the active-low reference model for the current START phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and a released-high external bus, then issue a STOP command after the START completes. Observe the initial released phase of START, the SCL release phase of STOP, and the final SDA release phase while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Release-side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain 0; whenever SCL or SDA is released, its corresponding output-enable is 1 (scl_oen=1 or sda_oen=1), allowing the modeled external pull-up to make that line high when no external participant drives it low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge during the START and STOP release phases, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0, verify output-enable polarity against the reference phase model, and verify a released, externally undriven line resolves high while an externally held-low line remains low.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, then issue a START command while scl_i and sda_i are externally released high. Observe the START sequence after each enabled timing tick, including the phase where SDA is driven low while SCL is high and the subsequent phase where SCL is driven low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the SDA-low START phase, sda_oen is low and the resolved SDA line is low despite the external pull-up; during the subsequent SCL-low phase, scl_oen is low and the resolved SCL line is low. The corresponding constant drive outputs remain low.
elements.check_method: At settled clocked observations, compare sda_oen=0 with resolved SDA=0 during the SDA-low phase and scl_oen=0 with resolved SCL=0 during the SCL-low phase using an open-drain bus model that resolves a line low whenever the DUT enable is low.

elements.stimulus: After completing the START command, issue a STOP command with ena=1 and keep the external SCL and SDA participants released high. Observe the STOP sequence through its final phase, after SCL has been released and SDA has also been released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: during the STOP release phases, scl_oen is high when SCL is released and sda_oen is high when SDA is released; with the external pull-ups released, both resolved I2C lines are high. A high output-enable must not actively pull its corresponding line low.
elements.check_method: At settled clocked observations, compare scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 with resolved SCL=1 and SDA=1 using an open-drain bus model, and verify that the high line levels are supplied by the external pull-ups rather than DUT drive.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the complete I2C master architecture using the specified module name and inspect the instantiated hierarchy.
elements.expected_response: The elaborated design contains i2c_master_bit_ctrl as the Bit Command Controller instance within the overall I2C master architecture, with its command, timing, bus-line, status, and data interfaces connected to the surrounding controller as defined.
elements.check_method: Run compile/elaboration and compare the generated hierarchy and connectivity report against the expected architecture; require an instance of i2c_master_bit_ctrl in the Bit Command Controller position with no unresolved or substituted module.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Present cmd=START=4'b0001 and hold the inputs until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen follow the START sequence: both are released initially, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released, and SCL is then driven low. The output-enable transitions occur only as commanded by the START sequence.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0 and compare scl_oen/sda_oen against a START-command reference model; require the observed release/drive phases and command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Present cmd=STOP=4'b0010 and hold the inputs until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen follow the STOP sequence: SDA is driven low, SCL is released, and SDA is released while SCL is high. The output-enable transitions occur according to the commanded STOP behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs after each posedge and compare scl_o/sda_o with constant 0 and scl_oen/sda_oen with the STOP reference model, including the required drive and release ordering.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, din=0, and present cmd=WRITE=4'b0100. Keep the external SDA line high whenever the DUT releases it and hold inputs until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen follow the WRITE sequence. SDA is driven low for din=0, SCL alternates between released high and driven low phases, and the enables return to the idle released state after completion.
elements.check_method: Use a WRITE reference model to compare every settled registered scl_oen/sda_oen value and phase ordering; independently assert scl_o=sda_o=0 throughout and require normal command completion without arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, sda_i=1, din=1, and present cmd=WRITE=4'b0100. Keep SDA high during the released high phase and hold inputs until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen follow the WRITE sequence for din=1. SDA is released rather than driven low, SCL is released during the high phase and driven low during the low phase, and the command completes normally.
elements.check_method: Compare settled output-enable waveforms with the din=1 WRITE reference model, verify the active-low polarity of each enable, and assert that the constant drive outputs remain 0 and no arbitration loss occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Present cmd=READ=4'b1000, return a stable external SDA value of 1 during the released read window, and hold inputs until completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0007: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen follow the READ sequence. SDA remains released for the read window, SCL is released for sampling and then driven low, and the enables return to idle after completion.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen/sda_oen at each settled posedge with the READ reference model and verify the release/drive phase ordering; independently check scl_o=sda_o=0 throughout.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Present cmd=NOP=4'b0000 and keep cmd=NOP for multiple enabled clocks; then repeat with unsupported cmd values 4'b0011 and 4'b1111.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0007: no command-controlled SCL or SDA sequence occurs. scl_o and sda_o remain 0, and scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the released idle values of 1; they do not change to drive either line low and no command completion is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor the output enables over the entire idle interval and compare them with the reset/idle reference model; require scl_o=sda_o=0, scl_oen=sda_oen=1, and no command-sequence transition for each no-op command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START (0001), and provide a released-high SCL and SDA bus. Hold the command until the controller accepts it, then continue driving the bus as required until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the START bit-level sequence: both lines are initially released, SDA is asserted low while SCL remains released/high, and SCL is subsequently asserted low. cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock at sequence completion.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard keyed from command acceptance to the cmd_ack pulse; compare the observed scl_oen and sda_oen phase ordering and polarity against the START reference sequence, and verify one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START or otherwise establish a busy transaction, then set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=STOP (0010) and issue it while the bus is available. Continue driving SCL high when released until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the STOP bit-level sequence: SDA is asserted low, SCL is released and allowed to become high, then SDA is released while SCL is high. cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock at sequence completion.
elements.check_method: Capture scl_oen and sda_oen on each settled posedge from STOP acceptance to cmd_ack and compare the ordered phases with the STOP reference model; verify no phase is skipped and ack is one clock wide.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (1000), provide a released SDA bus, and drive SCL through a valid low-to-high-to-low read bit cycle. Hold the command until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the READ bit-level sequence: SDA remains released, SCL is released for the read window, and SCL is subsequently asserted low before completion. cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock after the read bit sequence.
elements.check_method: Compare the recorded output-enable trace against the READ reference sequence, requiring SDA release during the read window, SCL release before its high phase, SCL assertion for the low phase, and a single cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE (0100), drive din=0 for the write bit, and provide a bus that remains consistent with the master's driven value. Hold the command until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: from command acceptance through cmd_ack, scl_oen and sda_oen show the WRITE bit-level sequence: SDA is driven low for din=0, SCL is released for the high phase, and SCL is then asserted low for completion. cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock and no arbitration abort occurs.
elements.check_method: Use a WRITE reference model to compare the ordered scl_oen and sda_oen phases and active-low enable polarity; verify din=0 drives SDA, the command reaches cmd_ack, and no unexpected abort occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0011 (unsupported), keep the bus released-high, and observe for at least the maximum expected command-acceptance interval.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the unrelated idle state and do not show any START, STOP, READ, or WRITE bit-level phase sequence; cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: While in idle, assert that no output-enable transition attributable to a command occurs and that no cmd_ack pulse is observed; compare the trace with the idle reference state rather than any command sequence.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the i2c_master_bit_ctrl DUT with its complete module port list, without applying runtime stimulus.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: module elaboration succeeds and the interface contains cmd, cmd_ack, busy, al, din, dout, scl_i, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_i, sda_o, and sda_oen; cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen are declared output ports.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator/compiler elaboration database or a port-introspection script to compare the exact port names and directions against the required interface; require zero elaboration errors.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate an otherwise identical interface-mutant DUT in which each observed output-port condition is tested negatively in separate mutations: remove cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, or sda_oen, or change one such port to an input.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: elaboration must fail or interface validation must reject the DUT because the affected port is absent or is not declared as the required output port; the corresponding 'otherwise' side of each observed_via shows clause is reported.
elements.check_method: Run compilation/elaboration and an interface-schema checker for every mutant, and compare diagnostics or introspection results against the expected missing-port or wrong-direction error; require rejection of every mutant.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT from its source and inspect the complete i2c_master_bit_ctrl port list, including cmd, cmd_ack, busy, al, din, dout, scl_i, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_i, sda_o, and sda_oen.
elements.expected_response: The interface elaborates successfully. cmd is a 4-bit input; cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, and sda_oen are scalar outputs; and din, scl_i, and sda_i are scalar inputs. This is the side of the requirement showing the specified port declarations.
elements.check_method: Use a compile-time RTL parser or elaboration API to compare every named port's existence, direction, and width against the required signature; record a passing bin for the conforming interface.

elements.stimulus: Run static interface checks against a deliberately nonconforming DUT variant in which at least one required declaration is changed, such as making cmd_ack an input, changing cmd from 4 bits to 1 bit, or making scl_oen a multi-bit port.
elements.expected_response: Static interface verification fails and identifies the absent, non-scalar, incorrectly directed, or incorrectly sized port. This is the contrasting side of the requirement: cmd_ack is absent, non-scalar, or declared with a different direction (and analogously for any altered required port), so the specified port behavior is not shown.
elements.check_method: Apply the same parser/elaboration signature comparison as TP-0000 and require a mismatch diagnostic for each injected declaration error; record a failing bin for every mutation.

elements.stimulus: Operate with ena=1 and nReset=1, issue a valid START command with clk_cnt=0, and wait until the command-complete pulse makes cmd_ack=1. Then assert rst=1 and hold it through the next rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding-case side of the observation: cmd_ack is driven low on the rising edge of clk as part of synchronous reset, and remains low while rst is held high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk, sample cmd_ack after registered updates settle; compare against a reference model that applies synchronous reset only on the rising edge and assert that cmd_ack transitions to 0 at that edge.

elements.stimulus: Operate with ena=1 and nReset=1, issue a valid START command with clk_cnt=0, and wait until cmd_ack=1. Assert rst=1 midway between two rising edges of clk, without changing clk or nReset, and observe cmd_ack before the next rising edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding-case side of the observation: before a rising edge of clk, asserting rst does not immediately change cmd_ack; cmd_ack retains its prior value of 1 until the next rising edge.
elements.check_method: Sample cmd_ack immediately after rst assertion between clock edges and again after the next posedge; verify it is unchanged before the edge and is cleared only after the posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt set to 0 so the command reaches its terminal phase promptly; monitor cmd_ack continuously before, during, and after completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cmd_ack asserts only on a rising edge of clk for the one-clock completion pulse. It remains unchanged between rising edges; any assertion or other value change between rising edges is a failure of synchronous updating.
elements.check_method: Use an edge-sensitive monitor sampling cmd_ack continuously and at every posedge clk; record the first cycle in which cmd_ack becomes 1 and fail if its value changes at any non-posedge time.

elements.stimulus: Complete a valid STOP command with ena high, then continue running for several clk cycles while monitoring cmd_ack continuously through the completion pulse and following idle cycles.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cmd_ack returns low only on a rising edge of clk after its one-clock completion pulse and then remains low between rising edges. The contrasting non-holding side—cmd_ack changing from 1 to 0, or otherwise changing value, between rising edges—must never occur and is a failure.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack at high-resolution simulation sampling points against its previous value and associate every transition with the immediately preceding posedge clk; fail on any transition not coincident with a rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset, issue a valid START command with ena high, and wait until the active START sequence drives scl_oen low. Assert rst high between two rising edges of clk, then hold rst high through the next rising edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case: asserting rst between clock edges does not immediately change scl_oen; on the next rising edge while rst is high, the synchronous reset takes effect and scl_oen becomes 1, releasing SCL.
elements.check_method: At a sample taken after the rst assertion but before the next clk rising edge, compare scl_oen against its pre-reset value of 0. At the following rising edge, sample scl_oen after sequential logic settles and require it to be 1.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset, issue a valid START command with ena high, and wait until the active START sequence drives scl_oen low. Keep rst low across multiple rising edges of clk while the command remains active.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: because rst is low, synchronous reset is not asserted and scl_oen remains governed by the active command sequence; it remains low while that phase is active rather than being reset to 1.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen after each of several rising edges with rst low and confirm it remains 0 until the command itself changes the output-enable state; specifically, do not accept a reset-induced transition to 1.

elements.stimulus: With rst low, execute a valid START or WRITE sequence until the controller is active and at least one output-enable is low; establish busy high and al high using a filtered START followed by a WRITE with din=1 and externally held SDA low during its released high phase. Assert rst high before a rising edge of clk and keep it high through that edge.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge with rst high, the synchronous reset side of shows applies: cmd_ack, busy, and al are cleared low, and scl_oen and sda_oen are set high, releasing SCL and SDA. The command FSM, counters, filtered inputs, and other internal state are reset; no command progress from the pre-reset operation is retained.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs immediately after the reset rising edge and compare cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. Use the reference model and subsequent enabled-clock behavior to confirm the FSM and timing/filter state restart from reset initialization rather than continuing the interrupted command.

elements.stimulus: Drive the same active-command setup, including busy high and al high, but keep rst low at a rising edge of clk while the command/status state is present. Do not assert either reset input.
elements.expected_response: At that rising edge the non-reset side of shows applies: rst does not clear cmd_ack, busy, or al and does not force scl_oen or sda_oen high. In particular, busy and sticky al remain high when their ordinary behavior requires them to remain set, and the controller does not perform synchronous-reset initialization.
elements.check_method: Compare post-edge outputs against the pre-edge ordinary-operation state and the reference model: verify al remains high and busy is not reset low, and verify output enables are not forced to the reset values solely because a clock edge occurred with rst low. Check that any command/FSM and counter progression follows normal enable/timing rules.

elements.stimulus: Run the DUT to a non-reset state with scl_oen=0, then drive nReset from 1 to 0 between clk rising edges while holding clk stopped and keep nReset low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows: immediately after nReset falls, before any subsequent clk posedge, scl_oen becomes 1; sda_oen also becomes 1 and cmd_ack, busy, and al become 0.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous waveform assertion sampled immediately after the nReset falling edge and before the next clk posedge; compare scl_oen and the corroborating reset outputs against their reset values with zero clock-edge latency.

elements.stimulus: Run the DUT to a non-reset state with scl_oen=0, keep nReset high, hold clk without a rising edge, and make no other input changes.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of shows: nReset remaining high does not asynchronously change scl_oen to 1; scl_oen remains 0 until a synchronous reset or normal clocked circuit behavior changes it.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen throughout a no-clock interval while nReset remains high and assert that it has no transition to the reset value; separately verify that no transition is attributed to nReset alone.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command with clk_cnt=1 and released-high SCL/SDA bus conditions. Keep ena high until the command reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the timed START sequence progresses and cmd_ack produces exactly one clock-high completion pulse after the command completes.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare cmd_ack against a reference model of the divider and START FSM; require progression only on enabled timing ticks and exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported START command with clk_cnt=1. Once the command is active but before its terminal phase, drive ena=0 for several clocks, then drive ena=1 until completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: while ena is low, timing progression is gated, cmd_ack remains low, and command completion is postponed; after ena returns high, the sequence resumes and cmd_ack produces one completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model with ena gating; assert no state or cmd_ack completion advance during the disabled interval and check the single delayed pulse after re-enable.

elements.stimulus: After reset with SCL externally high and SDA initially high, set ena=1 and hold the bus stable long enough for synchronizer/filter settling. Then drive SDA stably low while keeping SCL high, allowing the filter to process the START-shaped transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: filter progression occurs, the stable filtered START transition is detected, and busy rises after the registered detection update.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronizers, filter sampling, majority histories, and START detector; compare the predicted filtered transition and busy update at each posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset with SCL externally high and SDA initially high, set ena=0 and drive SDA stably low while keeping SCL high for multiple filter intervals. Then set ena=1 and hold the transition until filter settling completes.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: while ena is low, filter progression is gated and busy does not change despite the otherwise qualifying SDA transition; after ena is re-enabled, filtering resumes and busy rises when the filtered START is detected.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for filter-enable gating and majority filtering; assert busy remains unchanged throughout the disabled interval and then matches the delayed filtered START detection after re-enable.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, issue a supported WRITE command with ena high until the command is accepted and the write sequence is active, then drive ena low and hold it low across multiple clk_cnt expiration points and the expected command-terminal interval; keep the bus response normal.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the cmd_ack observation: cmd_ack remains low and the active WRITE command does not complete while ena is 0. Timing progression and FSM advancement are paused or gated.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after settled registered updates, assert that cmd_ack is 0 and the active-command probe remains in the WRITE sequence or otherwise does not reach its terminal acknowledgement phase for the duration of ena=0; compare against a reference divider/FSM model.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release it, issue the same supported WRITE command with ena held high through the complete command, and keep the bus response normal.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high contrast for cmd_ack: with ena at 1 and the command reaching its terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on settled posedge clk samples and compare its assertion cycle with the reference model's terminal WRITE phase; require one and only one high cycle and no missing acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it with the bus idle and SCL high. Drive a stable SDA high-to-low transition while ena is low, then hold ena low long enough to exceed the synchronizer and filter intervals.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the busy observation: busy remains low because input-filter progression and filtered START processing are gated while ena is 0.
elements.check_method: Sample busy and the filter_sample_tick/start_condition probes after each settled posedge; require no filter sampling or filtered START detection attributable to the transition and require busy to remain 0 throughout ena=0.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and release it with the bus idle and SCL high. Drive the same stable SDA high-to-low transition with ena high and hold the bus levels long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to complete.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high contrast for busy: with ena at 1, the filtered START is detected and busy rises.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict the filtered SDA transition and sample busy after settled posedge clk updates; require start_condition followed by busy=1, with latency consistent with the enabled filter progression.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue a supported START with ena high, wait until a START phase is established with scl_oen at its current phase value, then drive ena low and hold it across at least two expected divider-expiration opportunities while keeping clk_cnt nonzero.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen remains at the established phase value and does not make the next timed START-sequence transition while ena is low, demonstrating that the divider reload and filter-counter reset prevent normal bit-timing progression.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while ena is low, compare scl_oen and the command-phase probe against a reference model with the divider reloaded and filter counter reset; assert that no next phase transition occurs.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset and supported START sequence, establish the identical START phase, but keep ena high across the next expected divider-expiration opportunity with the same clk_cnt.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen advances from the established phase to the next expected START-sequence SCL phase when the divider expires, unlike the ena-low holding case.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model and compare the observed scl_oen transition and phase probes after each posedge; require the transition within the modeled enabled timing interval.

elements.stimulus: Reset with the bus idle (scl_i=1, sda_i=1), drive ena low, then drive sda_i low and hold SCL high and SDA low for enough clocks to span multiple potential filter-sampling opportunities.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy does not assert from the stable filtered START condition while ena is low, because filter progression is reset/gated; busy remains at its preexisting low value.
elements.check_method: Sample busy after each settled posedge and compare the filter-history and filtered-edge reference model with ena-low sampling disabled/reset; assert no busy transition and no start_condition event.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the reset and idle-bus setup with ena high, then drive sda_i low while scl_i remains high and hold the transition stable through the modeled synchronization and filter interval.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the filtered START is eventually detected and busy asserts high, demonstrating that filter progression occurs when ena is high.
elements.check_method: Compare busy and start_condition against a reference model for the two-stage synchronizer, filter sampling, and majority transition; require busy to assert at the modeled filtered START processing clock.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd4, then issue a START command while the bus inputs are released high. Continue clocking until the command sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the divider loads clk_cnt, asserts clk_en at the reference-model expiration points, and the START FSM advances only on those clk_en ticks. No command phase advances between enabled ticks.
elements.check_method: At every posedge, compare the observed clk_en_asserted probe and command-state progression against a reference divider/FSM model initialized with clk_cnt=4; verify each phase transition is coincident with a modeled clk_en tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd0, then issue a START command on an enabled clock and continue clocking through the command sequence.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case boundary: the zero prescale value is loaded without wedging the divider; clk_en_asserted occurs on every enabled clock, and the START FSM advances on each such tick.
elements.check_method: Compare clk_en_asserted and the observed FSM probes with a reference model using zero-reload semantics and a minimum one-enabled-clock tick interval; flag any missing tick or FSM transition not caused by another modeled wait condition.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=0 and clk_cnt=16'd4, apply a START command and hold it for multiple clocks, then later set ena=1 without changing the command.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast: while ena=0, the divider does not generate clk_en_asserted and the FSM remains idle without accepting START. After ena becomes 1, divider timing resumes from the specified reload behavior and the command may advance only on subsequent clk_en ticks.
elements.check_method: Monitor clk_en_asserted and in_idle on every posedge; require no clk_en tick or FSM transition during the ena=0 interval, then compare post-enable ticks and transitions with the reference divider/FSM model.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and run for at least 12 rising edges of clk. Repeat the measurement after reset if needed to exclude initialization effects.
elements.expected_response: Holding/derived side of shows: with clk_cnt equal to zero, filter_sample_tick is asserted on every enabled clock after reset initialization; the SDA/SCL filter sampling interval is therefore one enabled clock and does not become stuck waiting for a nonzero divider.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the filter counter and compare every post-initialization filter_sample_tick probe assertion with the DUT on each posedge clk; additionally check that the maximum interval between successive ticks is one enabled clock.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0010, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and run for at least 40 rising edges of clk. Record filter_sample_tick assertions after reset initialization, then repeat with clk_cnt=16'h0008 without changing any other input.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: for nonzero clk_cnt, filter_sample_tick does not occur every enabled clock; its spacing follows the clk_cnt-derived filter interval. With clk_cnt=16'h0010 the interval is floor(16/4)=4 enabled clocks, and changing clk_cnt to 16'h0008 changes it to floor(8/4)=2 enabled clocks.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed filter_sample_tick cycle numbers against a reference model using filter_interval=floor(clk_cnt/4), with the documented minimum one-clock behavior; verify the measured tick spacing is four enabled clocks for 16'h0010 and two for 16'h0008, allowing only the defined first-sample initialization offset.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, deassert it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, then drive cmd=4'b0001 (I2C_CMD_START) while the FSM is idle and hold it through the next rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: The idle command decoder recognizes START and the FSM enters the START command sequence; in_start_sequence becomes asserted. This is the holding side of the observation: when REQ-0021 holds, the START-sequence indication is present.
elements.check_method: After each posedge clk and settled registered updates, sample the in_start_sequence probe and compare against a reference FSM model; require the probe to assert after command acceptance and the FSM not to remain idle.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, deassert it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'h0000, then drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) while the FSM is idle and hold it through multiple rising edges of clk.
elements.expected_response: The command does not select the START sequence: in_start_sequence remains deasserted and the FSM remains idle with no START-sequence progression. This is the contrasting side of the observation: when REQ-0021's START-decoding behavior is not activated, the START-sequence indication is absent.
elements.check_method: At every enabled posedge, sample in_start_sequence and in_idle and compare with the reference FSM model; require in_start_sequence=0 and in_idle=1 throughout the observation window.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and establish an idle, released bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and cmd=4'b0010 (I2C_CMD_STOP); hold the command until it is accepted, then provide the released-high SCL condition required for STOP completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observation: because cmd=2 is the supported STOP encoding, sda_oen first drives low, then returns high after scl_oen has been released high, producing the STOP waveform.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor sda_oen and scl_oen with a protocol checker. Confirm the ordered transitions sda_oen=0, followed by scl_oen=1, followed by sda_oen=1, and confirm the sequence completes once without remaining in the idle released value.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and establish an idle, released bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and cmd=4'b0011, an unsupported command encoding; hold it for multiple enabled clocks while keeping the FSM idle.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of the observation: because cmd=3 is not the supported STOP encoding, sda_oen remains at its idle released value of 1 and does not produce the STOP-specific low-then-release sequence.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_oen and scl_oen after every posedge for the observation interval. Assert that sda_oen remains 1, no STOP low phase occurs, and no transition sequence sda_oen=0 then 1 is observed.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the controller idle with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=4 (I2C_CMD_WRITE), din=0, and model the external bus as released high whenever the DUT releases it. Keep cmd at 4 until the WRITE sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: The value 4 is accepted as a supported WRITE command. The WRITE sequence executes to its terminal phase and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock; no arbitration loss occurs.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor cmd_ack and the in_write_sequence/in_idle probes. Confirm that a WRITE sequence is entered and that exactly one one-clock cmd_ack pulse occurs after the terminal WRITE phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the controller idle with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and drive cmd=3 (an unsupported command encoding) for at least the duration required for a command sequence to complete under the same conditions.
elements.expected_response: The unsupported value is not treated as I2C_CMD_WRITE: the FSM remains idle and cmd_ack never pulses high. This is the non-holding side of the observed behavior, where no WRITE completion pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: Sample cmd_ack and in_idle on each settled posedge for the full observation window. Assert that in_idle remains asserted, no active command probe is entered, and cmd_ack remains low throughout.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, then drive ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, and cmd=4'b1000 (I2C_CMD_READ) while the FSM is idle; hold the command through the next enabled clock tick and provide a released-high bus.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting recognized-command side of the requirement: the FSM leaves idle and enters the READ command sequence, indicated by in_read_sequence=1 and in_idle=0; it must not remain in idle as an unsupported command would.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset release, sample in_idle and in_read_sequence after nonblocking updates; assert that the first command-acceptance tick causes in_read_sequence to assert and in_idle to deassert, using the reference model for the enabled tick.

elements.stimulus: For each cmd value 4'b0000, 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111, reset the DUT to idle, then drive ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, and the selected cmd while holding it through at least two enabled clock ticks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting idle/unsupported-command side of the requirement: the FSM remains in idle for every selected command, with in_idle=1 and in_read_sequence=0 throughout; no READ sequence is entered and no command-completion pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Run one independently reset transaction per command value and compare sampled in_idle, in_read_sequence, and cmd_ack against the reference model on every posedge after nonblocking updates; require in_idle to remain asserted and cmd_ack to remain low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and din=0, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) while the FSM is idle, and keep the external SDA/SCL bus responses normal so the WRITE sequence proceeds. Observe the WRITE data-bit phase, including its released high phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 0, which is the din=0 side of the required behavior; the transmitted zero is driven low on SDA.
elements.check_method: When the in_write_sequence probe identifies each WRITE data-bit phase, compare the registered sda_oen value during the stable transmitted-data phase against the expected value 0 and record a passing bin for din=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and din=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) while the FSM is idle, and keep the external SDA/SCL bus responses normal, including SDA high during the released WRITE high phase so arbitration is not lost. Observe the WRITE data-bit phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 1, which is the din=1 side of the required behavior; SDA is released to transmit a high bit.
elements.check_method: When the in_write_sequence probe identifies the WRITE data-bit phase, compare the registered sda_oen value during the stable transmitted-data phase against the expected value 1 and record a passing bin for din=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=0, issue the WRITE command cmd=0100, and provide a normal released-high SCL/SDA bus so the WRITE operation reaches its data-driving phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-driving phase, including the released high phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, so the DUT drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: At every registered phase transition of the WRITE operation, sample sda_oen after the posedge and assert that it is 0 while din=0 in the data-driving and released-high phases; also verify the externally modeled SDA line is low when no external participant overrides it.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive din=1, issue the WRITE command cmd=0100, and provide a normal released-high SCL/SDA bus so the WRITE operation reaches its data-driving phase.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-driving phase, including the released high phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, so the DUT releases SDA high. This is the din=1 side of the requirement's shows condition; sda_oen=0 for this case would be the contrasting nonconforming behavior.
elements.check_method: At every registered phase transition of the WRITE operation, sample sda_oen after the posedge and assert that it is 1 while din=1 in the data-driving and released-high phases; also verify the externally modeled SDA line is high when no external participant drives it low.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate the DUT behind an I2C open-drain pad model. Exercise the external SCL line with both states: release all external drivers so the pulled-up line is high, then assert an external participant's low drive so the resolved line is low.
elements.expected_response: The DUT's scl_i input equals the resolved external I2C SCL line in each state: high when the line is released and low when the external participant drives it low.
elements.check_method: At every sampled testbench clock event, compare the resolved pad/bus value with the DUT scl_i port using a cycle-accurate immediate assertion; record separate coverage bins for resolved-high and externally-driven-low states.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue a WRITE command with ena high, release SCL for the write high phase, and externally hold scl_i low. Keep scl_i low until the synchronized and majority-filtered SCL becomes high, then allow the high phase and following low phase to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: cmd_ack remains low while the released SCL is observed low through the synchronized and filtered input, the timing counter and active write phase do not advance, and cmd_ack pulses only after filtered SCL becomes high and the remaining write phase completes.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling interval, three-sample majority filter, slave-wait condition, and FSM timing; compare slave_wait_active, fsm_active, scl_oen, and cmd_ack against the model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue a WRITE command with ena high, release SCL for the write high phase, and apply a short scl_i low-to-high or high-to-low pulse that is shorter than the synchronizer/filter acceptance interval; then leave scl_i at the expected high level.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the raw SCL glitch is rejected by synchronization and filtering, so no false slave-wait release or timing transition occurs, the write high phase is not completed from the glitch, and cmd_ack occurs only according to the normal filtered-SCL timing.
elements.check_method: Record raw scl_i, synchronized stages, filter histories, filtered SCL, slave_wait_active, clk_en_asserted, and cmd_ack; assert that the glitch produces no filtered SCL transition and that the observed command timing matches the filtered reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue a command that releases SCL, and while scl_i is released high drive an external SCL falling edge. Hold the low level long enough to pass synchronization and filtering, then release scl_i high and wait for the next filtered high level.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the accepted filtered falling edge asserts clock synchronization, reloads the timing counter, and causes subsequent bit timing to use the synchronized and filtered SCL behavior rather than the raw edge.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_sync_active, filter_sample_tick, filtered SCL transitions, timing-counter reload, clk_en_asserted, and command-phase progression with a reference model that includes synchronizer and filter latency.

elements.stimulus: During an active command with SCL released high, inject an scl_i falling edge shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval and restore scl_i high before a filtered falling edge can form.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the raw SCL edge does not assert clock synchronization, does not reload the timing counter, and does not alter the active command timing or phase progression.
elements.check_method: Use waveform assertions and a filter reference model to verify no filtered SCL falling edge and no scl_sync_active pulse occur, and compare timing-counter and FSM traces with a no-glitch run.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue START with ena high while the external bus is high, then drive SDA from high to low and hold both scl_i high and sda_i low long enough for synchronization and filtering to accept the transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy changes high only after filtered SDA falls while filtered SCL is high; the START condition is detected from filtered signals rather than raw inputs.
elements.check_method: Compare synchronized/filter histories, filtered_scl_high, start_condition, and registered busy against a reference model, allowing the modeled synchronization and filter latency.

elements.stimulus: After establishing busy high, keep scl_i low or inject a short raw SDA high-to-low or low-to-high glitch that does not survive synchronization and filtering; do not apply a stable filtered bus transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy remains unchanged; no START or STOP condition is detected when the raw SDA transition occurs while filtered SCL is low or when the transition is rejected by filtering.
elements.check_method: Assert that start_condition and stop_condition remain inactive for the rejected transition and that registered busy does not change; compare against the three-sample filtered SCL/SDA reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue READ with ena high, release SDA and SCL for the read window, drive a stable SDA value, and drive scl_i through a low-to-high transition held long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL rising edge to be accepted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout updates to the filtered SDA value on the accepted filtered SCL rising edge, and the READ command proceeds to its low phase and eventually generates cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for SCL synchronization, filter majority, and rising-edge detection; check that dout changes on the modeled filtered_scl_rising event, not on the raw scl_i edge, and that cmd_ack follows the modeled READ sequence.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, issue READ with ena high, release SDA with dout initialized to a known value, and inject a raw scl_i rising pulse too short to create a synchronized and filtered rising edge; return scl_i low or hold it below the filter threshold.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout does not update for the rejected raw SCL pulse, and no READ sampling event is generated until a valid filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rising and dout with an assertion that dout remains at its prior value whenever no filtered rising edge is present; compare the result with the synchronizer/filter reference model.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. With filtered SCL high, drive sda_i stably from high to low and hold it long enough for two-stage synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to produce a filtered SDA falling transition. Do not issue a command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy asserts only after the synchronized and filtered SDA falling transition is detected while filtered SCL is high; it does not assert at the raw sda_i transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizers, filter histories, and majority value. Compare the modeled filtered SDA transition and busy assertion cycle with the DUT busy output; verify no earlier busy assertion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 with filtered SCL high. Starting from stable filtered SDA high, drive a low pulse on sda_i shorter than the synchronization/filter settling requirement, then return sda_i high before the filtered SDA majority value changes.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy remains unchanged; the raw SDA glitch does not create a synchronized and filtered SDA falling transition and therefore does not trigger START detection.
elements.check_method: Predict synchronizer and three-sample majority histories with the reference model and confirm that filtered SDA has no falling edge and the DUT busy output has no corresponding change.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy=1 with a valid filtered START. Keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold filtered SCL high, then drive sda_i stably from low to high for enough clocks to pass synchronization and majority filtering.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy clears only when the synchronized and filtered SDA rising transition is detected as STOP while filtered SCL is high; it does not clear at the raw SDA transition.
elements.check_method: Run the reference synchronization/filter model, identify the filtered SDA rising edge, and compare its predicted STOP processing cycle and busy deassertion with the DUT.

elements.stimulus: Establish busy=1 with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low. Apply a short high pulse on sda_i that ends before synchronization and filtering can produce a filtered SDA rising transition, then restore sda_i low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy remains asserted; the short raw SDA pulse does not produce a filtered STOP transition and does not clear busy.
elements.check_method: Compare the DUT filtered-transition behavior, using the reference filter model or filter_sample_tick probe, against busy. Require no filtered SDA rising edge and no busy deassertion.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a WRITE command with din=1. During the released-high WRITE phase, drive sda_i stably low long enough for synchronization and filtering to make filtered SDA low while filtered SCL is high and sda_arbitration_check is active.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: al asserts when the synchronized and filtered SDA is low during the released-high arbitration-check phase, the active WRITE aborts without cmd_ack, and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronization/filter model to locate filtered SDA low and compare it with sda_arbitration_check, al, cmd_ack, and sda_oen/scl_oen. Require al assertion only after the filtered value is available.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a WRITE command with din=1. During the released-high arbitration-check phase, apply an SDA-low pulse shorter than synchronization/filter settling and return sda_i high before the filtered SDA value becomes low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: al remains deasserted and the WRITE is not aborted because the synchronized and filtered SDA does not indicate arbitration loss; no false arbitration-loss response is generated by the raw glitch.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronizer and majority filter, verify filtered SDA never becomes low while sda_arbitration_check is active, and compare DUT al, cmd_ack, and command completion against the no-loss reference path.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a READ command with SCL initially low. Drive sda_i stably low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SDA value to become low, then release SCL and create a filtered SCL rising edge while SDA remains low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout updates to 0 on the filtered SCL rising edge, using the synchronized and filtered SDA value rather than the raw input transition timing.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to determine the filtered SDA value and filtered SCL rising-edge cycle. Compare DUT dout at that registered edge and verify it captures 0.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a READ command and arrange for filtered SDA to be stably high before the read sampling window. At the time of the filtered SCL rising edge, drive raw sda_i low only briefly, returning it high before the synchronized and filtered SDA value changes.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout captures 1 at the filtered SCL rising edge and does not capture the brief raw low value; an unsynchronized or unfiltered SDA glitch has no effect on read data.
elements.check_method: Predict synchronized SDA, majority-filtered SDA, and filtered SCL rising-edge timing with the reference model. Require DUT dout to equal the modeled filtered SDA value of 1, not the instantaneous raw sda_i value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START while the FSM is idle; provide released-high SCL and SDA and allow the complete START sequence to run to its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: When the START sequence completes, cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle, then returns low and does not remain asserted or generate an additional pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a command-sequence reference model to identify the terminal START edge and compare sampled cmd_ack after each posedge: require cmd_ack=1 on exactly that completion cycle and cmd_ack=0 on the preceding and following cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle; begin with a busy transaction state and provide SCL high so the complete STOP sequence can finish.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP sequence completes, cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle, then returns low with no second completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Model the STOP phase progression and terminal edge, then use a cycle-accurate assertion that cmd_ack is high on the terminal edge only and is low for all other cycles in the transaction window.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ while the FSM is idle; release SDA, provide a defined external read bit on SDA, allow filtered SCL to rise and then fall, and let the complete READ sequence finish.
elements.expected_response: At completion of the READ bit-level sequence, cmd_ack asserts high for exactly one clk cycle and is low before and after that cycle.
elements.check_method: Use the divider/filter/READ reference model to locate the completion edge despite variable latency, and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform against a one-cycle pulse at that edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=WRITE while the FSM is idle; drive din=1, allow the external bus to remain high during the released SCL phase, and provide normal SCL high and low phases until the WRITE sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: When the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts and does not repeat.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE command using a protocol reference model, identify its terminal phase, and check cmd_ack with a one-cycle pulse assertion aligned to completion and no pulses during intermediate phases.

elements.stimulus: Issue a valid WRITE command with ena=1, then drive ena=0 while the command is in an active phase before completion and hold it low for multiple clk cycles; do not allow the command to reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: because the command has not completed, cmd_ack does not assert as a one-clock-cycle completion pulse during the ena-low interval.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that no command-completion edge occurs while ena=0, then assert cmd_ack remains low on every sampled clock in that interval and that no spurious pulse is emitted.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave ena high, keep the filtered bus idle with SDA and SCL high, then drive a stable SDA high-to-low transition while SCL remains high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to assert start_condition.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered START detection event, busy becomes high on the following registered status update and remains high until a STOP is detected. This is the busy-high side of the requirement; it must not remain low after START.
elements.check_method: Monitor start_condition and busy after nonblocking assignments settle on each posedge. Assert that busy is 0 before the registered update, 1 on the posedge immediately following start_condition processing, and remains 1 until a later STOP event.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy high using a stable filtered START, then while busy is high drive a stable SDA low-to-high transition with SCL remaining high long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to assert stop_condition.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP detection event, busy becomes low on the following registered status update. This is the busy-low contrasting side of the requirement; it must not remain high after STOP.
elements.check_method: Monitor stop_condition and busy after nonblocking assignments settle on each posedge. Assert that busy is 1 before the registered update, 0 on the posedge immediately following stop_condition processing, and remains 0 afterward unless another START is detected.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the filtered bus idle with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high. Drive a stable SDA high-to-low transition while SCL remains high, maintaining it long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to assert start_condition.
elements.expected_response: On the registered cycle processing the filtered START condition, busy becomes high and remains high. This is the 'busy is high after START detection' side of the required port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered START detection cycle, then sample busy after that posedge and assert busy==1; verify it remains high until a subsequent filtered STOP.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy high with a stable filtered START. Then, with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low, drive a stable SDA low-to-high transition and maintain it long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to assert stop_condition.
elements.expected_response: On the registered cycle processing the filtered STOP condition, busy becomes low and remains low. This is the 'busy is low after STOP detection' side of the required port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered STOP detection cycle, then sample busy after that posedge and assert busy==0; verify the preceding START established busy==1.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and during the released-high WRITE phase drive the external SDA line low while SCL is high so the filtered SDA becomes low during arbitration checking.
elements.expected_response: The al output asserts on the clock edge processing the arbitration failure; this is the asserting side of the observed_via shows statement. al remains high thereafter until reset.
elements.check_method: After the filtered SDA-low arbitration-check event, compare al against a reference model on each clock and verify it changes from 0 to 1 and remains 1 until reset.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and keep the external SDA line high throughout the released-high WRITE phase so arbitration checking observes released SDA high.
elements.expected_response: al does not newly assert because the arbitration-loss condition is absent; with no prior arbitration loss it remains low. This is the non-asserting side of the observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered SDA and arbitration-checking interval, then compare al with a reference model and require al=0 through command completion, assuming no prior loss.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command, and while the command is active and SCL is filtered high, drive filtered SDA from low to high to create an unexpected STOP condition; do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: The al output asserts on the clock edge processing the unexpected STOP; this is the asserting side of the observed_via shows statement. al remains high thereafter until reset.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered SDA/SCL reference model to identify the STOP edge while the command FSM is active and non-STOP, then compare al and verify assertion on that edge and retention until reset.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command, and complete the command without generating an SDA rising transition while filtered SCL is high and without issuing a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: al does not newly assert because no unexpected STOP occurs; with no prior arbitration loss it remains low. This is the non-asserting side of the observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: Track filtered START/STOP events and command activity with a reference model, and require al=0 for the complete command when no arbitration-loss condition occurs.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle, allow the READ sequence to reach its data-bit capture phase, drive the filtered SDA value low, and generate a filtered SCL rising edge during that phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0034: on the registered update following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout equals the received filtered SDA data bit, 0.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value, then compare dout after the corresponding posedge update against 0.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue cmd=1000 (READ) while idle, allow the READ sequence to reach its data-bit capture phase, drive the filtered SDA value high, and generate a filtered SCL rising edge during that phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0034: on the registered update following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout equals the received filtered SDA data bit, 1.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value, then compare dout after the corresponding posedge update against 1.

elements.stimulus: First complete a READ capture that establishes a known prior dout value, then return the command FSM to idle and create a filtered SCL rising edge with a changed filtered SDA value while no READ data-bit capture phase is active.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of REQ-0034: dout is not required by this requirement to equal the current received or filtered SDA bit; retaining its prior value is permitted, and no equality requirement is applied outside the READ capture condition.
elements.check_method: Confirm with the reference model and in_read_sequence probe that the filtered SCL rising edge occurs outside the READ capture phase; do not compare dout to the changed SDA value or flag either retention or another DUT-defined value as a violation of REQ-0034.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command on an enabled timing tick. Allow the controller to release SDA and SCL for the read window; drive the external SDA line to 1, then produce a stable filtered SCL low-to-high transition while maintaining SDA=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when filtered_scl_rising is asserted, dout updates on the corresponding clock edge to 1, the current filtered SDA value.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rising and sample dout after the same posedge clock update; compare dout with the reference-model three-sample majority filtered SDA value and require equality on the rising-edge event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a READ command. During the released read window, hold SCL low so no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, and change the external SDA line from 0 to 1 while allowing SDA filtering to settle; do not create a filtered SCL low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because filtered_scl_rising is not asserted, dout does not update to the current filtered SDA value and retains its previous captured value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that no filtered SCL rising event occurs during the SDA change, then assert that dout remains equal to its value before the change throughout the interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and observe scl_o and scl_oen throughout the START sequence while the external SCL line remains released high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_o is low at every clock-edge observation, including while scl_oen is high and the DUT releases SCL; scl_o does not change from low.
