elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, assert scl_o===1'b0 and record scl_oen transitions to confirm observations include the released-SCL phase.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START, then issue a STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0; observe scl_o and scl_oen through the STOP sequence as scl_oen changes from driving SCL low to releasing SCL high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: even when scl_oen is low and the DUT drives SCL low, scl_o remains low and never becomes high or changes from low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, assert scl_o===1'b0 across both scl_oen=0 and scl_oen=1 intervals; flag any high value or transition on scl_o.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and issue the START command (cmd=0001) on a clock edge; continue clocking until the START sequence reaches its phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 0; this is the 'shows' side of REQ-0037@1 indicating that the SCL line is driven low. With open-drain bus modeling, the resolved SCL line is low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, monitor in_start_sequence and sample scl_oen. When the START sequence is in its SCL-low phase, assert scl_oen==0 and compare the resolved SCL line against low in the open-drain reference model.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously and release it without issuing a command; keep ena high, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1 while clocking several cycles in idle.
elements.expected_response: While idle and not executing an SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 1; this is the 'otherwise' side of REQ-0037@1 indicating that the SCL line is released rather than driven low. With no external low driver, the resolved SCL line is high.
elements.check_method: After asynchronous reset and on subsequent settled posedges, assert in_idle==1 and sample scl_oen==1. Compare the resolved SCL line with high in the open-drain reference model and ensure no interval is incorrectly reported as driven low.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, then issue a START command with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external bus lines released high. Observe the registered outputs during the initial START phase after each posedge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen is 1, indicating that SCL is released for the external pull-up, and sda_o is 0. The external SCL line remains high when no participant drives it low.
elements.check_method: At every sampled output observation in the SCL-released START phase, assert scl_oen==1 and sda_o==0; additionally assert that the modeled open-drain SCL line is high when the external driver is released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external bus lines released high. Wait for the START sequence to progress from its released-SCL phase to the subsequent phase where the controller pulls SCL low, then observe the registered outputs after the corresponding posedge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen is 0, indicating that SCL is driven low rather than released, while sda_o remains 0 as its constant-low drive value.
elements.check_method: Use the command-sequence timing or in_start_sequence probe to identify the SCL-low phase, then assert scl_oen==0 and sda_o==0 at the settled registered output. Verify the modeled SCL line is low even with the external driver released.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=0 then release it, set rst=0 and ena=1, configure clk_cnt=0, release the external SDA and SCL lines high, and issue a START command. Advance clocks until the START sequence reaches its SDA drive phase.
elements.expected_response: During the START SDA drive window, sda_oen is 0, indicating the output enable is asserted, and the resolved open-drain SDA bus is driven low despite the external participant releasing SDA.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, monitor sda_oen and resolve SDA as low when sda_oen=0 or the external participant drives low, otherwise high. Confirm sda_oen=0 and resolved SDA=0 throughout the SDA drive window.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and release both external bus lines high. Issue a READ command and advance clocks until the READ data window in which the master releases SDA.
elements.expected_response: During the READ SDA release window, sda_oen is 1, indicating that SDA is released rather than driven low; with the external participant also releasing SDA, the resolved SDA bus remains high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge in the READ data window, compare sda_oen with the resolved open-drain SDA value. Confirm sda_oen=1 and resolved SDA=1 when no external device drives SDA low, demonstrating the contrasting non-drive behavior.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=STOP, and allow the STOP sequence to progress through driving SDA low, releasing SCL high, and reaching its final SDA-release phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the STOP sequence reaches its final phase with scl_oen already 1, sda_oen changes to and remains 1, releasing SDA so the external pull-up drives the SDA line high; cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock after STOP completion.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, monitor sda_oen, scl_oen, SDA line level, and cmd_ack. Assert that sda_oen=1 in the final STOP phase, the modeled open-drain SDA line is high when externally undriven, and cmd_ack is a one-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=STOP, and sample the initial STOP phase before the final SDA-release phase is reached.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: while the STOP sequence is driving SDA low, sda_oen=0 and the modeled SDA line is low; this is the non-release side of the specified observation, rather than the sda_oen=1 released-high behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the STOP-sequence phase probe and settled registered outputs to sample before the final SDA-release transition. Assert sda_oen=0 and SDA low during the initial STOP drive phase, then separately confirm the later transition to sda_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: Inspect the source-of-truth specification and confirm that the implementation-details section introduced by REQ-0041 is present; then run a minimal DUT smoke sequence consisting of asynchronous reset release followed by an idle NOP command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the specification contains the implementation-details section. No additional DUT output behavior is defined or required by this requirement; the smoke sequence produces the DUT's ordinary reset and NOP behavior.
elements.check_method: Source inspection verifies the section exists. A checker compares the smoke-trace outputs against the baseline reset/NOP reference trace and confirms that no REQ-0041-specific interface effect is claimed.

elements.stimulus: Create a specification-only mutation that removes the implementation-details section introduced by REQ-0041, while leaving the DUT source and its reset/NOP smoke stimulus unchanged.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting absent case: the implementation-details section is missing from the specification. No DUT port is expected to change, because REQ-0041 has no observable interface effect; the DUT smoke trace remains identical to the baseline.
elements.check_method: A document-lint check detects the missing section. Differential comparison of the DUT smoke trace against TP-0000 confirms identical outputs, documenting that the requirement is not distinguishable at any DUT port.

elements.stimulus: After reset, exercise idle, START, STOP, WRITE with din=0 and din=1, and READ command sequences with ena high while sampling scl_o and sda_o after every posedge clk.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case, scl_o is always 0 and sda_o is always 0 throughout reset, idle, and every command phase; line ownership is represented only by scl_oen and sda_oen, never by driving scl_o or sda_o high.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge observation, assert scl_o === 1'b0 and sda_o === 1'b0 for the complete test, including command transitions and completion.

elements.stimulus: During an otherwise valid command sequence, inject a design/output fault that drives scl_o high or sda_o high for at least one sampled clock edge, while leaving scl_oen and sda_oen observable.
elements.expected_response: For the non-holding case, the observed high value on scl_o or sda_o corresponds to the violation side of the observation: scl_o=1 indicates the module drives SCL high directly and sda_o=1 indicates the module drives SDA high directly; the requirement checker must flag the violation.
elements.check_method: Use an assertion sampled after each posedge clk: !(scl_o || sda_o). Confirm that forcing either output high causes the assertion to fail and identifies the offending port.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous and synchronous reset, then exercise ena high and low, clk_cnt values 0, 1, and 16'hFFFF, arbitrary cmd values including START, STOP, READ, WRITE, NOP, and unsupported encodings, while driving arbitrary scl_i and sda_i values.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_o shows 0 and sda_o shows 0 continuously, including during reset, at every sampled clock edge, and throughout all command and enable conditions.
elements.check_method: At reset observation and immediately after each posedge clk, sample scl_o and sda_o and assert both equal 1'b0; collect a bin for reset, idle, active-command, ena-low, and each prescaler class.

elements.stimulus: During reset, idle, and an active command, apply a testbench fault injection that overrides or corrupts scl_o and sda_o to 1'b1 for at least one sampled clock edge, then release the injection.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the observed port shows scl_o=1 and/or sda_o=1 while the fault is active, which is the 'otherwise' side of the requirement and must be reported as a violation of REQ-0043; after release, the DUT must again show both outputs as 0.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_o and sda_o during the injected interval and require the checker to flag any nonzero value against REQ-0043@1, then assert both return to 0 on subsequent samples after fault removal.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA lines, assert ena, issue a START command, and wait until the START sequence reaches its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SCL: scl_oen is low and the resolved SCL line is pulled low. The SDA control may remain at the value required by the START phase.
elements.check_method: At the settled clock edge for the SCL-low phase, compare scl_oen with the resolved open-drain SCL model and require scl_oen==0 and SCL==0.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA lines, assert ena, issue a START command, and observe the initial START window before the controller pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SCL: scl_oen is high and the resolved SCL line is released high because the controller does not pull it low.
elements.check_method: During the initial START window, compare scl_oen with the resolved open-drain SCL model and require scl_oen==1 and SCL==1 when the external participant is released.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA lines, assert ena, issue a START command, and observe the START phase in which SDA is asserted while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for SDA: sda_oen is low and the resolved SDA line is pulled low.
elements.check_method: At the settled clock edge for the SDA-low START phase, compare sda_oen with the resolved open-drain SDA model and require sda_oen==0 and SDA==0.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START command, then issue a STOP command with the external SCL and SDA lines released, and observe the final STOP phase after SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for SDA: sda_oen is high and the resolved SDA line is released high because the controller releases SDA.
elements.check_method: During the final STOP release window, compare sda_oen with the resolved open-drain SDA model and require sda_oen==1 and SDA==1 when the external participant is released.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, then run with ena high and issue a START command followed by a STOP command using clk_cnt=0. Model the external bus as pulled high unless the DUT output-enable for that line is low. Observe the START phase that pulls SDA low and the STOP/START phases that pull SCL low.
elements.expected_response: This is the low-drive side of the requirement: scl_o and sda_o remain 0, and whenever scl_oen=0 the modeled SCL line is low while whenever sda_oen=0 the modeled SDA line is low. The low output-enable must actively pull the corresponding line low rather than produce a high or high-impedance drive.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge observation during the command phases, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0; correlate each output-enable low value with a low modeled bus line and verify the corresponding line is not high despite the external pull-up.

elements.stimulus: After reset, run with ena high and clk_cnt=0. Issue START and then STOP while modeling both external lines as pulled high when released. Observe the START phase with SCL released, the STOP phase with SCL released, and the final phase with SDA released.
elements.expected_response: This is the released-side contrast: scl_o and sda_o remain 0, and whenever scl_oen=1 the modeled SCL line rises to the external pull-up level while whenever sda_oen=1 the modeled SDA line rises to the external pull-up level. Releasing an output-enable must not actively pull its corresponding line low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge observation in the released phases, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0, assert the relevant output-enable is 1, and compare the modeled bus line against the external pull-up high level; fail if the released line is driven low.

elements.stimulus: Apply no DUT stimulus; review Specification item 2 as a list-marker/scaffolding item with no activation condition, required output, or behavioral obligation.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output value, state transition, or test stimulus is required or inferred from Specification item 2.
elements.check_method: Static traceability review comparing the requirement text and normalized expectation against the generated testplan; confirm no functional DUT check is attributed to this item.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue a START command, and continue clocking through an active command while recording the internal timing counter, clk_en_asserted probe, and scl_oen/sda_oen outputs.
elements.expected_response: During each countdown cycle after a reload, cnt decrements and clk_en_asserted remains deasserted, so the command output enables do not advance to the next timing phase. When cnt reaches zero, cnt reloads from clk_cnt, clk_en_asserted asserts for that timing event, and the appropriate scl_oen or sda_oen command-phase transition becomes visible on the following registered output update. This is the holding case of the observed behavior: the next command-boundary event occurs at the expected countdown boundary.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model initialized from clk_cnt=3; compare cnt expiration and clk_en_asserted on every posedge, then compare the settled registered output enables against the predicted command phase after each tick.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, issue START on a released-high bus and sample the active command on the first two enabled clocks after a timing reload, before the counter reaches zero; do not alter scl_i or sda_i.
elements.expected_response: While cnt is nonzero, cnt decrements on each clock, clk_en_asserted remains low, and scl_oen/sda_oen remain in the current command phase rather than advancing. This is the contrasting non-holding case of the observed behavior: because the timing counter has not expired, no next command-boundary event occurs yet.
elements.check_method: Compare each sampled cycle with the divider reference model and assert that no command-phase output-enable transition occurs before the modeled expiration tick; also check that clk_en_asserted is low on those cycles.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt=0, release reset, set ena=1, keep the bus released high, issue START, and run several consecutive rising edges.
elements.expected_response: On every enabled clock, cnt reloads with zero and clk_en_asserted is asserted rather than becoming stuck in a decrementing state. The active command advances through its timing phases on successive enabled clocks, with scl_oen/sda_oen transitions occurring according to the START sequence.
elements.check_method: Compare the divider and command-phase trace against a zero-reload reference model; assert clk_en_asserted on every enabled clock and verify that output-enable phases progress without deadlock.

elements.stimulus: Start a command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, then drive ena=0 for multiple rising edges while the command is active; afterward drive ena=1 again and continue with the bus released high.
elements.expected_response: While ena is low, cnt is reloaded from clk_cnt and clk_en_asserted is asserted as specified for the disabled condition, while command acceptance and command-phase progression remain disabled; scl_oen and sda_oen do not advance through active command phases. When ena returns high, normal countdown and phase progression resume from the re-enabled timing sequence.
elements.check_method: At every posedge compare the counter/tick probes with the model's ena-disabled branch and compare output enables with a model that suppresses FSM advancement while ena is low; verify phase progression resumes only after re-enabling.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset asynchronously between clock edges while clk_cnt=5 and an active command is in progress; observe the divider and clk_en_asserted immediately, then release nReset and apply rst=1 for one rising edge before returning rst=0.
elements.expected_response: For either reset condition, cnt is loaded from clk_cnt and clk_en_asserted is asserted according to the reset branch. The command logic is reset to its initial phase with both output enables released, and after reset release the divider restarts from the loaded value rather than continuing the pre-reset countdown.
elements.check_method: Check asynchronous behavior immediately after nReset assertion and synchronous behavior after the rst posedge; compare the counter, clk_en_asserted probe, and settled scl_oen/sda_oen outputs against the reset-aware reference model.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, issue START and reach a phase in which scl_oen=1 and the controller has released SCL; hold the external SCL line high, then drive scl_i low long enough for the synchronized and filtered falling edge to assert scl_sync_active.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered falling edge is recognized during released SCL, cnt reloads from clk_cnt and clk_en_asserted is asserted for the synchronization event. The next command-boundary output transition is postponed until timing restarts from this synchronized edge, rather than occurring according to the stale countdown that preceded the edge.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filtering, counter reload, and command timing; correlate scl_sync_active and clk_en_asserted with the counter reload, and assert that scl_oen/sda_oen do not show the next phase transition before the restarted timing interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 asynchronously and release it, then set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=3, cmd=START, and model the bus as released-high initially. Accept the START command on an enabled timing tick. When the DUT releases SCL by driving scl_oen high during the active START sequence, externally hold scl_i low for at least four expected divider periods, then release scl_i high and allow the transaction to continue.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of REQ-0048: while released SCL remains low, cmd_ack does not pulse and command completion is postponed for the entire interval. After scl_i is released high and the remaining START sequence completes, cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock; no completion pulse occurs during the stretch.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard and reference divider model to identify the interval after scl_oen becomes high while filtered SCL remains low. Assert that cmd_ack is low on every clock in that interval and that the command terminal event is delayed until after filtered SCL becomes high. Confirm exactly one one-clock cmd_ack pulse after the resumed sequence completes; sample registered outputs after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 asynchronously and release it, then set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=3, cmd=START, and model the bus as released-high. Accept the START command and keep scl_i high whenever scl_oen is high, so no slave clock stretching occurs.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0048: because released SCL is observed high, cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock at the normal START terminal phase, without the additional delay that occurred in the stretched case.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference timing model with no slave-wait interval and compare the observed cmd_ack cycle against the predicted terminal cycle. Assert no extra wait cycles beyond divider, filtering, and synchronization latency, and assert that cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: Provide the specification list-item marker "3." to the requirement normalizer and testplan generator.
elements.expected_response: The item is classified as imposing no requirement and generates no DUT behavioral expectation, stimulus, or output assertion beyond retaining its traceability reference.
elements.check_method: Inspect the normalized requirement and generated testplan metadata; compare against expectation="no output behavior is required" and verify that no DUT signal check is emitted.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid READ command, provide the normal preceding phase until scl_oen transitions from 0 to 1, then hold scl_i=0 for at least the full synchronizer and filter settling interval and for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case: after scl_oen rises to release SCL while filtered SCL remains low, the slave-wait behavior holds the command in the released-SCL phase; scl_oen remains 1, command outputs do not advance, and cmd_ack remains low with no completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, majority filtering, divider, and command phases. Detect the scl_oen rising edge, confirm filtered SCL is still low, then assert that cmd_ack is continuously low and that no terminal command phase or acknowledgement occurs while scl_i remains low.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid READ command, provide the normal preceding phase until scl_oen transitions from 0 to 1, hold scl_i=0 long enough to establish the released-SCL wait, then drive scl_i=1 and keep it high through synchronization and majority-filter settling.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: once filtered SCL becomes high after the released-SCL wait, the command progresses through its remaining phases and cmd_ack produces exactly one clock-wide completion pulse; the acknowledgement is postponed during the low filtered-SCL interval and is not generated during that interval.
elements.check_method: Compare the DUT against a cycle-accurate reference model. Confirm cmd_ack is low while filtered SCL is low after scl_oen rises, then after the modeled filtered-SCL rising transition confirm the expected command progression and exactly one cmd_ack pulse with no duplicate or early pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (4'b1000), and keep sda_i high. Accept the command, then externally hold scl_i low throughout the phase in which the READ sequence releases SCL; continue clocking until the synchronized and filtered SCL value remains low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: scl_oen becomes 1 while the externally held-low SCL line remains low, and slave_wait_active asserts. The READ timing counter and bit-level FSM remain paused until filtered SCL becomes high; no phase completion is required while the hold persists.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for command acceptance, synchronization, filtering, and clk_cnt=0 timing. At the first released-SCL phase, check registered scl_oen=1 and compare slave_wait_active with the model after filter settling; assert that it is 1 on each enabled clock while filtered SCL is low and that the FSM does not advance.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (4'b1000), and keep sda_i high. Accept the command and externally release scl_i high before and throughout the READ phase in which the master releases SCL; continue clocking through filter settling and the subsequent high phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: scl_oen becomes 1 and filtered SCL becomes high rather than remaining low; slave_wait_active remains 0, so the timing counter and bit-level FSM continue advancing without a slave-wait pause.
elements.check_method: Use the same reference model for synchronization, filtering, and timing. Check that registered scl_oen=1 during the released-SCL phase, filtered SCL reaches 1, slave_wait_active never asserts for that phase, and the FSM advances on subsequent clk_en ticks.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=1 with the bus initially released and high. Issue a valid START command. When the controller releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1) during the START sequence, externally hold scl_i low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL value to remain low across multiple timing-counter expirations.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in REQ-0052: while slave_wait_active is asserted, scl_oen remains 1 and the transition to the next SCL-low phase is postponed; the timing counter produces no effective FSM advance despite enabled-clock opportunities.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, filtering, divider expiration, and slave-wait entry. After scl_oen is released and filtered SCL is low, compare scl_oen on every posedge for several clk_en opportunities and assert that it remains high and that no next-phase transition occurs until filtered SCL becomes high.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, initially released-high bus, and valid START command sequence, but when the controller releases SCL during the START sequence, leave scl_i high so the synchronized and filtered SCL value reaches high before the next timing opportunity.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting normal case in REQ-0052: because filtered SCL is released high, scl_oen advances from the released state to the next SCL-low phase at the normal timing opportunity rather than remaining postponed.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate reference model and compare the observed scl_oen transition against the first eligible clk_en after filtered_scl_high becomes 1. Assert that scl_oen changes to 0 at that opportunity, contrasting with the held-low case.

elements.stimulus: Apply any legal clocked stimulus, including reset, enable, command, and bus inputs, while recording the DUT outputs.
elements.expected_response: No specific DUT output behavior is required or asserted for this requirement.
elements.check_method: Mark the scenario covered if the test executes; perform no value comparison or pass/fail assertion on DUT outputs.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena=1, and a valid clk_cnt, issue a START command and allow the command FSM to reach a phase where scl_oen=1 and the filtered SCL is high. While SCL remains released, have the external bus participant pull scl_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to produce a filtered SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: when the filtered SCL falling edge occurs while scl_oen=1, scl_sync_active asserts for the detected synchronization event and the timing behavior responds as a synchronized externally forced SCL fall.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for the two-stage SCL synchronizer, filter sampling interval, majority filter, and filtered falling-edge detection. At the cycle where the model produces the filtered falling edge, compare the scl_sync_active probe against 1 and verify that it is not asserted before that filtered edge.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena=1, issue a START command and allow the FSM to transition from its released-SCL phase into the phase that drives SCL low, observing scl_oen=0. Ensure the filtered SCL was high immediately before the master drive-low action, then allow scl_i and the filtered SCL to fall and remain low long enough to produce a filtered falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting, non-holding side of the requirement: because the falling filtered SCL edge occurs while the controller is driving SCL low (scl_oen=0), scl_sync_active remains deasserted; no multi-master clock-synchronization event is reported.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered SCL high-to-low edge and sample scl_oen at that edge. Assert that scl_oen=0 and compare the scl_sync_active probe with 0 for the edge cycle and the subsequent normal low phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue a valid READ command on a released-high bus, and do not externally force a filtered SCL falling edge while the active command has scl_oen=1. Hold scl_i high and allow the scheduled timing boundary to occur.
elements.expected_response: The no-forced-edge side of the requirement applies: scl_oen remains released during the high phase and transitions low at the scheduled command timing boundary.
elements.check_method: Use a divider/filter reference model to predict the scheduled timing boundary; sample scl_oen after each posedge and assert that it transitions from high to low at that boundary, with no synchronization-induced postponement.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue a valid READ command on a released-high bus, wait until the active command has scl_oen=1, then have another bus participant drive scl_i low long enough for the synchronized, majority-filtered SCL value to make a falling transition before the master's scheduled low-phase boundary.
elements.expected_response: The forced-edge side of the requirement applies: the falling filtered-SCL event indicates another master forced SCL low; scl_oen remains high rather than transitioning low at the original scheduled boundary, and the timing interval is reloaded so the low-phase transition is postponed.
elements.check_method: Monitor the synchronized/filter reference model and scl_sync_active probe to identify the filtered falling edge, then compare scl_oen against the model after each posedge. Assert scl_oen stays released through the synchronization reload and that the subsequent low transition occurs later than the original scheduled boundary.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt. Issue a WRITE command and drive din=0. During the released-high WRITE phase, while scl_oen=1, drive the shared SCL low long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a falling filtered SCL edge, then release SCL high so the command can continue.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the falling filtered SCL edge while SCL is released, the timing counter reloads and the low-period timing restarts from that synchronized edge. Consequently, scl_oen remains 1 beyond the ordinary local transition point and changes to 0 only after the restarted low-period timing interval expires.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider, synchronizer, filter, and FSM reference model. Align the observed falling filtered SCL edge with the model's reload event, then compare the observed scl_oen transition to the model-predicted postponed transition; assert that it does not occur at the unresynchronized local schedule.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same enabled WRITE transaction, clk_cnt, din, and released-high phase timing, but keep the shared SCL high so no falling filtered SCL edge occurs while scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no falling filtered SCL edge occurs while SCL is released, scl_oen transitions to 0 on the ordinary local bit-timing schedule without the additional counter reload or restarted low-period delay.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model with synchronization disabled for this scenario and compare the observed scl_oen transition cycle against the ordinary local schedule. Cross-check that the transition occurs earlier than, or at the model's unsynchronized point rather than the postponed point from TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: Provide the implementation-details source artifact containing an entry explicitly labeled item 5, then run the requirement-identification or specification-import flow.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish an idle bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, ena=1, and busy=0. Drive sda_i from 1 to 0 while keeping scl_i=1, then sample busy on each posedge of clk before the raw transition has propagated through the two-stage synchronization and filtering pipeline.
elements.expected_response: The raw SDA transition is not reflected immediately: busy remains at its previous value of 0 before the synchronized and filtered START condition is reached. This is the non-propagated side of REQ-0058's observed_via shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for cSDA/cSCL synchronization and filtering to determine the first cycle on which a filtered START can occur; assert that busy remains 0 on all earlier sampled cycles and that no immediate raw-input response occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish an idle bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, ena=1, and busy=0. Apply a stable START transition by holding scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 for sufficient clk rising edges for both synchronization stages and the filtering pipeline to complete.
elements.expected_response: After the stable scl_i and sda_i values have traversed the two-stage synchronization and filtering pipeline, busy changes from 0 to 1 when the corresponding filtered START condition is reached. This is the propagated side of REQ-0058's observed_via shows behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled busy against a reference model that captures scl_i and sda_i through two sequential synchronization stages and then applies the specified filtering and START detection; require busy to remain 0 before the modeled filtered START and to rise on the modeled detection cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i high, hold sda_i high long enough to establish initialized high filter histories, then drive sda_i stably low and keep it low. Allow the synchronizer, filter counter, and filter sampling interval to run while recording filter_sample_tick timing and busy.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy rises only after enabled filter-sampling opportunities have elapsed and sufficient synchronized samples have been shifted into the fSDA history to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high. busy must not rise on the raw or merely synchronized SDA transition before those sampling opportunities.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizer, filter-counter reload/expiry, sample-shift events, three-sample majority, and START detection. Assert that busy's registered rising edge occurs no earlier than the modeled qualifying filter sample and that it follows the modeled filtered START transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set clk_cnt=8, hold scl_i high and sda_i high, set ena=0, then drive sda_i stably low for multiple clock cycles spanning several would-be filter intervals. Keep ena=0 throughout the observation window.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because filter progression is disabled, no filter samples are shifted into the fSCL or fSDA histories and busy does not rise for the SDA transition, even though the raw and synchronized SDA inputs are low. No START indication may be reflected at busy until ena is reasserted and the required filter sampling and qualification occur.
elements.check_method: Compare against a reference model with filter-counter progression and sample shifts suppressed while ena=0. Sample busy after each settled posedge and assert it remains low throughout the disabled interval; optionally reassert ena and verify busy rises only after the subsequently modeled qualifying filter samples.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, and leave the bus filtered-high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the synchronized three-sample SCL and SDA histories have majority value 1. Then drive sda_i low long enough for at least two consecutive filter-sample updates while keeping scl_i high, and continue clocks until the synchronized histories update.
elements.expected_response: The majority-filtered SCL remains 1 and the majority-filtered SDA changes from 1 to 0. This is the holding side of REQ-0060's observation: busy rises to 1, evidencing a START detected from the majority-filtered SCL and SDA values.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample histories, and majority function. At each settled posedge compare the modeled filtered values with the START condition and sample busy after registered updates; require busy to assert once when modeled filtered SDA falls while modeled filtered SCL is high.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and establish synchronized three-sample SCL and SDA histories with majority value 1, keeping scl_i high. With ena high and clk_cnt set to 0, drive sda_i low for only one synchronized filter-sample update and then return sda_i high, so the SDA history contains at most one low sample and its majority remains 1; keep scl_i high throughout.
elements.expected_response: The majority-filtered SDA remains 1 and the majority-filtered SCL remains 1. This is the non-holding side of REQ-0060's observation: busy does not rise because the SDA glitch is too short to change the corresponding three-sample majority value.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer/filter reference model to confirm the SDA history never has two low samples at once and that the modeled majority outputs remain high. Monitor busy after every settled posedge and require no busy assertion or START indication during and after the glitch.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value with a known filter sampling interval. Establish idle bus conditions with filtered SCL high, filtered SDA high, and busy low. Apply an SDA low pulse shorter than the majority-filter acceptance window, then restore SDA high before enough synchronized samples can produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: This is the short-glitch side of the busy observation: busy remains low; the SDA glitch does not produce a filtered START condition or change bus status.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage synchronizer, filter sample ticks, three-sample majority history, and filtered edge detection. At every settled posedge, compare the modeled filtered SDA/START result and busy output; require no busy assertion during or after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value with a known filter sampling interval. Establish idle bus conditions with filtered SCL high, filtered SDA high, and busy low. Drive SDA low and hold it long enough for the synchronized samples and three-sample majority filter to accept the transition, then hold the resulting START condition long enough for detection.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-glitch contrasting side of the busy observation: busy rises after the sustained SDA high-to-low transition produces a filtered START condition.
elements.check_method: Predict the filtered SDA transition and START event with the reference synchronizer/filter model, then compare busy after each posedge, allowing the modeled synchronization and filter latency. Require busy to assert exactly when the filtered START is processed.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, initialize dout=0, issue and accept a READ command with ena=1, establish stable filtered SDA=1 during the read data-bit capture phase, and release SCL. Apply an SCL pulse shorter than the majority-filter acceptance window, returning SCL low before enough synchronized samples can produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the short-glitch side of the dout observation: dout retains its previous value of 0 because the SCL glitch produces no filtered SCL rising edge and therefore no read capture.
elements.check_method: Drive the READ sequence using the command FSM and compare raw-line samples, synchronized histories, filtered SCL edges, and dout against the reference model on settled posedges. Require no modeled or observed filtered SCL rising edge and no dout update during the pulse.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, initialize dout=0, issue and accept a READ command with ena=1, establish stable filtered SDA=1 during the read data-bit capture phase, and release SCL. Hold SCL low until the filter accepts it, then drive SCL high long enough for the synchronized samples and three-sample majority filter to produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-glitch contrasting side of the dout observation: dout updates from 0 to the filtered SDA value 1 when the sustained SCL transition produces a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to determine the accepted filtered SCL rising-edge cycle, then compare dout after each settled posedge. Require dout to become 1 on the registered cycle that processes that filtered rising edge, with no earlier update.

elements.stimulus: Reach specification list item 6; apply no additional DUT stimulus.
elements.expected_response: No output behavior, state transition, timing constraint, or other DUT response is required by this requirement.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement-to-test trace and confirm that the scenario records no behavioral assertion beyond the absence of an obligation.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and establish filtered SDA=1 and filtered SCL=1. Drive sda_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to produce a filtered SDA falling edge, while keeping scl_i high so filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SDA falling edge is processed with filtered SCL high, start_condition is asserted. This is the 'when the condition holds' side of the START-detection behavior, equivalent to ~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL.
elements.check_method: At each filter_sample_tick, compare the observed start_condition probe against a reference model of the synchronized three-sample majority filter and the predicate (~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL); require assertion only on the modeled filtered SDA falling edge with filtered SCL high.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and establish filtered SDA=1 and filtered SCL=0. Drive sda_i low and hold it long enough for synchronization and filtering to produce a filtered SDA falling edge, while keeping scl_i low so filtered SCL remains low.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA falling edge must not assert start_condition because filtered SCL is low. This is the 'when the condition does not hold' side of the START-detection behavior.
elements.check_method: At each filter_sample_tick, compare start_condition with the reference predicate (~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL); require it to remain deasserted for the modeled filtered SDA falling edge when filtered SCL=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive scl_i high and sda_i low long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low. Then hold scl_i high and drive sda_i high long enough for a filtered SDA low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA rising transition while filtered SCL is high asserts stop_condition for the corresponding sampled detection event. This is the holding case of the STOP predicate.
elements.check_method: Use the filter/synchronizer reference model to identify the cycle where sSDA=1, dSDA=0, and sSCL=1; compare the stop_condition probe with sSDA && !dSDA && sSCL on that cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, establish filtered SDA low and filtered SCL low with ena=1, then drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i low until the filtered SDA low-to-high transition is observed. In a separate repetition, establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, then drive sda_i low and high again only after the filtered value has settled, ensuring the tested high phase has no filtered SDA rising transition.
elements.expected_response: stop_condition remains deasserted when filtered SDA rises while filtered SCL is low, and also remains deasserted when filtered SCL is high but filtered SDA does not make a low-to-high filtered transition. This is the non-holding case of the STOP predicate.
elements.check_method: Use the filter/synchronizer reference model to locate each candidate sample and assert that stop_condition is 0 whenever !(sSDA && !dSDA && sSCL); verify no probe pulse occurs in either negative subcase.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT and execute a representative idle-clock trace with reset asserted and released, ena both low and high, and cmd driven through NOP, START, STOP, READ, WRITE, and unsupported values.
elements.expected_response: No behavior, output value, timing, or state transition is required by REQ-0065; the trace must not be interpreted as imposing any additional DUT requirement.
elements.check_method: Review the generated assertion and coverage database to confirm that this requirement has a traceability entry but no DUT behavior assertion or output comparison is attributed to it.

elements.stimulus: Release both bus lines and hold filtered SCL high with filtered SDA high, then drive SDA low long enough for the majority filter to detect a filtered START while SCL remains high. After START detection, keep the bus active without generating a STOP for multiple clocks.
elements.expected_response: The busy output becomes high after the registered processing of the filtered START condition and remains high throughout the START-to-STOP window. This is the high side of the requirement's stated behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and START detection. At each settled posedge, compare busy with the model and verify busy remains high from the detected filtered START until a filtered STOP occurs.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then keep the filtered bus idle with SCL high and SDA high without generating a filtered START. In a second phase, optionally create a filtered STOP transition while busy is low, and continue holding the bus idle.
elements.expected_response: busy remains low when no START-to-STOP window is active, including after reset and after a STOP detected while busy is low. This is the low side of the requirement's stated behavior.
elements.check_method: Model reset, synchronization, filtering, and START/STOP edge detection; sample busy after each settled posedge and compare it against the expected low value whenever the model has no active START-to-STOP window.

elements.stimulus: Exercise the DUT with a representative valid command and bus sequence, then compare behavior against the requirements other than REQ-0067.
elements.expected_response: The DUT exhibits only the behavior specified by the independently defined requirements; no additional output, state transition, timing rule, or interface obligation is attributable to REQ-0067.
elements.check_method: Review the trace against the requirements baseline and assert that no extra checker, output expectation, or coverage bin is required for the numbered-list marker itself.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1, issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1, and provide a released-high bus. When the accepted WRITE sequence reaches its stable high phase with sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1, externally hold SDA low long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to make filtered SDA low while SDA arbitration checking is active.
elements.expected_response: At the clock processing the filtered SDA-low arbitration observation, al asserts. It remains asserted for subsequent clocks, the WRITE command aborts without cmd_ack, and the controller releases both SDA and SCL.
elements.check_method: Use the sda_arbitration_check and filtered_sda_low probes to identify the qualifying phase; sample al after each posedge and compare against a reference model. Require an al rising transition on the qualifying observation, sticky al thereafter, and no cmd_ack for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al low, set ena=1, issue the same WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1, and provide a released-high bus. During the stable high WRITE phase with sda_oen=1, keep external SDA high long enough for the filtered SDA value to remain high throughout the active SDA arbitration-checking window; allow the WRITE bit to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: Because the released-high expectation is not contradicted, al does not newly assert as a consequence of the arbitration-checking condition. The WRITE sequence proceeds to its normal completion and produces its ordinary cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the sda_arbitration_check and filtered SDA probes to delimit the arbitration window; verify al remains low from reset through that window and compare the phase progression and cmd_ack against the normal-write reference model.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT so al=0. With ena=1, issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 from idle with din=0. elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command, wait until the command is active with SCL released high, then drive SDA low and subsequently high while SCL remains high for sufficient enabled filter samples to produce a filtered STOP condition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle. Drive the external bus so SDA is released by the DUT and presents a stable filtered value of 0, then allow a filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sampling window; repeat a READ sampling window with stable filtered SDA=1 and another filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: on each filtered SCL rising edge during the READ data-bit sampling window, dout updates to the current filtered SDA value—0 for the first sample and 1 for the second sample—and the READ command subsequently produces cmd_ack.

At every modeled filtered SCL rising edge, compare the post-posedge registered dout value with the modeled filtered SDA value, and verify each captured value remains observable until the next sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=READ with ena=1. During the READ sampling window, arrange for one filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is 0, then change SDA sufficiently early for the filter to produce a stable filtered value of 1 before the next filtered SCL rising edge. Keep both edges within the same READ operation and wait for cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: dout must not retain or report the previous sample at the second edge. It captures the current filtered SDA value at each edge, yielding dout=0 after the first filtered SCL rising edge and dout=1 after the second; behavior in which dout does not capture the current filtered SDA value is a failure.
elements.check_method: Predict filtered SDA and filtered SCL with the synchronization/filter reference model, identify two successive filtered SCL rising edges, and compare dout immediately after each corresponding posedge against the modeled current filtered SDA. Explicitly flag a stale, early, raw-input, or otherwise mismatched second sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled timing tick. Drive the external bus so the filtered SDA value is 0, then produce a stable filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sequence; repeat with filtered SDA=1 on the next READ bit's filtered SCL rising edge. Allow synchronization and majority filtering to settle before each edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on each rising edge of filtered SCL during the READ sequence, dout updates after the registered-output clock update to the corresponding filtered SDA value, first 0 and then 1, so the byte controller can collect both received bits.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority value, and filtered SCL edge detection. At each modeled filtered SCL rising edge, sample dout after the posedge NBA update and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value; require the observed update before the READ command's cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled timing tick. During the READ sequence, hold filtered SCL low or high without creating a filtered SCL rising edge while changing the external SDA value and allowing the SDA filter to settle; then create a filtered SCL falling edge or maintain the same filtered SCL level, but do not create a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not provide a newly captured READ bit at that phase or edge; dout retains its previous registered value and no new READ-bit capture is reported before the next qualifying rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter and edge model to identify cycles with no filtered SCL rising edge. Sample dout after each posedge and assert that it remains equal to its prior value despite SDA changes; separately verify that any subsequent dout change is attributed only to a modeled filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive clk_cnt=3, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and then continue clocking while keeping ena=1 and the bus inputs stable. elements.check_method: Use a reference divider model to predict clk_en from clk_cnt and ena. At each settled posedge, compare the current scl_oen/sda_oen values and phase signature with the preceding clock; require no phase transition on every cycle for which the model predicts clk_en=0, excluding reset and abort conditions.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive clk_cnt=3, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and continue clocking without reset, arbitration loss, or clock-stretching. Drive the sequence through a timing-phase boundary and wait for the reference divider to expire and assert clk_en.

elements.check_method: Predict clk_en and the expected START phase sequence with a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model. Compare settled scl_oen and sda_oen outputs at each posedge, requiring the first phase transition to coincide with the modeled clk_en assertion and requiring the expected next phase afterward.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=4'b0010 (STOP), and apply the next rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: On the enabled timing tick, the FSM leaves idle and enters the STOP command sequence; in_stop_sequence asserts and in_idle deasserts.
elements.check_method: At the settled outputs after the rising edge, compare the in_stop_sequence and in_idle probes against the expected values using a transition coverage bin for STOP acceptance.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=4'b1000 (READ), and apply the next rising edge of clk.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP), and apply the next rising edge; repeat with an unsupported encoding such as cmd=4'b0011.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and provide a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, and the in_start_sequence probe on every posedge until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: once the START sequence begins, scl_oen and sda_oen follow the START timing phases: both lines initially release, SDA is driven low while SCL remains released/high, then SCL is driven low before completion. sda_chk remains inactive. Each registered enable transition is visible one clock after the corresponding FSM phase transition, and cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse at sequence completion.
elements.check_method: At settled post-posedge sampling points, compare the ordered scl_oen/sda_oen values against a START-sequence reference model and require the in_start_sequence interval to contain the expected phases and no sda_chk assertion.

elements.stimulus: After establishing a busy transaction, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=STOP, and provide scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 when the bus is released. Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, and the in_stop_sequence probe until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during STOP, SDA is driven low first, SCL is released and allowed high, then SDA is released while SCL is high. scl_oen and sda_oen match those phase-specific values, sda_chk remains inactive, and cmd_ack pulses once after the terminal STOP phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-by-cycle scoreboard keyed to in_stop_sequence and filtered SCL level; compare both output-enable polarities and verify exactly one completion pulse after the expected phase ordering.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ. Keep the external bus released, return sda_i=1 for one read bit, and provide scl_i=1 during the released SCL read window, followed by scl_i=0 when the controller pulls SCL low. Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, in_read_sequence, and filtered_scl_rising until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: READ releases SDA throughout the read bit, releases SCL for the high/read window, captures the returned SDA value on the filtered SCL rising edge, then drives SCL low before acknowledging. The output enables follow this phase order and sda_chk remains inactive.
elements.check_method: Score the registered output-enable sequence against the READ reference model, correlate the released-SCL interval with in_read_sequence and filtered_scl_rising, verify dout=1, and require one cmd_ack after the low phase.

elements.stimulus: From idle with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1. Keep sda_i=1 so arbitration succeeds, and allow scl_i to be high when SCL is released and low after the high phase. Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, in_write_sequence, and sda_arbitration_check until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: WRITE drives or releases SDA according to din=1, releases SCL for the stable high phase, asserts SDA arbitration checking during that released high phase, then drives SCL low and acknowledges once. No arbitration loss occurs.
elements.check_method: Compare each registered scl_oen/sda_oen value with the WRITE phase model, require sda_arbitration_check only during the released high phase, and verify no al assertion plus exactly one cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Repeat a WRITE from idle with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, but set din=0; hold sda_i=0 during the driven-low phase and provide normal SCL high/low timing. Sample scl_oen, sda_oen, in_write_sequence, and sda_arbitration_check until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: din=0 causes SDA to be driven low during the WRITE data phase, SCL is released and then driven low in the required order, and SDA arbitration checking is not used as a released-high expectation for this zero bit. The command completes with one cmd_ack and no al.
elements.check_method: Match output-enable polarity and phase ordering against a din=0 WRITE reference sequence; assert that no false arbitration loss or missing completion occurs solely because filtered SDA is low.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and apply cmd=NOP, then each unsupported 4-bit command encoding other than 0000, 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000 while the bus remains released-high. Hold each value for several enabled clocks and observe scl_oen, sda_oen, all sequence probes, sda_arbitration_check, and cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE sequence is active, scl_oen and sda_oen remain at their released idle values (1,1), no phase-specific drive/release sequence or SDA arbitration checking occurs, all command-sequence probes remain inactive, and cmd_ack stays low.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed outputs and probes with the idle reference model for every unsupported command and NOP; flag any departure from (scl_oen,sda_oen)=(1,1) or any sequence activity as a failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and the bus released/high, issue cmd=0001 (START), and allow every required clk_en timing tick to occur without reset, clock stretching that prevents completion, or arbitration loss. Continue until the START sequence reaches its terminal timing phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the FSM transitions from the active START sequence to in_idle, and cmd_ack is asserted high for exactly one clk cycle at completion, then returns low while in_idle remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate scoreboard keyed to clk_en and the in_start_sequence/in_idle probes. At the terminal transition compare the registered cmd_ack value to 1, require it to be 0 on the immediately preceding and following clocks, and require in_idle to be 1 after completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1, and during the released high phase of a WRITE bit externally hold SDA low while filtered SCL is high. Allow the arbitration-loss response to complete.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: arbitration loss aborts the active sequence before its terminal completion phase; the FSM returns to in_idle and cmd_ack does not assert for that aborted command, so there is no one-clock completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_arbitration_check, al, in_write_sequence, in_idle, and cmd_ack in the clocked waveform. Confirm al asserts, the active WRITE sequence exits to in_idle, and cmd_ack remains low throughout the abort and subsequent idle cycles; flag any cmd_ack pulse as a failure.

The sequence then changes scl_oen=0 while SDA remains driven low, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock at the terminal START phase.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked reference model keyed to command acceptance and clk_en ticks. At every settled posedge, assert the required phase ordering and mutual output-enable values; verify the SDA-low phase occurs before scl_oen becomes 0, and detect exactly one cmd_ack pulse after the SCL-low phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the FSM idle and both external bus lines high, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled clocks; do not issue a START command.
elements.expected_response: The START behavior does not occur: sda_oen and scl_oen remain released high, no SDA-low-while-SCL-high START phase is created, SCL is not pulled low by a START sequence, and cmd_ack remains low. This is the contrasting non-holding side of the requirement's observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack after each settled posedge for the observation window. Assert that no release-to-SDA-pull-low transition, no SCL pull-low transition, and no command-complete pulse occurs while the NOP is applied.

elements.stimulus: After reset, release both bus lines externally high, set ena=1 and cmd=START (4'b0001), and hold these inputs until the START sequence reaches the phase where sda_oen=0 while scl_oen is still 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the phase immediately after SDA is pulled low while SCL is high, scl_oen changes to 0, pulling SCL low; at the following command-complete edge cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence probe and sampled registered outputs after each posedge. Assert that scl_oen=1 during the SDA-low/SCL-high phase, then scl_oen=0 in the next START phase, and that cmd_ack is high for one clock only with no additional pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset with both bus lines externally high, set cmd=START (4'b0001) while ena=0 and hold ena low for several clocks, then return cmd to NOP.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the START sequence is not accepted, so scl_oen remains 1 and SCL is not pulled low; cmd_ack remains low and no completion pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: Observe in_idle and sample scl_oen and cmd_ack after each posedge while ena=0. Assert that no START-sequence probe becomes active, scl_oen stays released at 1, and cmd_ack never asserts.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=0010 (STOP) with ena=1 on a clock-enable opportunity and keep the external SCL line released high; run until cmd_ack asserts.
elements.expected_response: The STOP sequence exhibits the required side of the observed behavior: sda_oen becomes 0 to drive SDA low, then scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL, and finally sda_oen becomes 1 while scl_oen remains 1, completing the STOP sequence.
elements.check_method: At settled posedge observations, use a temporal assertion or reference-model phase comparison to require the ordered output-enable sequence sda_oen=0, then scl_oen=1, then sda_oen=1 with scl_oen=1 before the single cmd_ack pulse; allow variable intervals between phases due to clk_en timing.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle after reset, issue cmd=0000 (NOP) with ena=1 for multiple clock-enable opportunities and do not issue a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, non-holding side of the observed behavior is present: no STOP sequence occurs, sda_oen does not transition to 0 as the STOP's SDA-low phase, scl_oen does not undergo the STOP release transition, and no STOP-specific ordered transition ending with sda_oen=1 while scl_oen=1 is observed; cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen and scl_oen over the complete stimulus window and assert that the ordered STOP signature from TP-0000 is absent, while confirming in_idle remains asserted and cmd_ack is never asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP while the FSM is idle. Model the open-drain bus released high, allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL high, then release SDA high while filtered SCL is high. Continue clocking through the terminal phase and subsequent idle clock.
elements.expected_response: At the terminal phase after SDA is released high while SCL is high, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock as the STOP command-complete pulse (the 'shows' side of the requirement). cmd_ack is low on the preceding and following clocks.
elements.check_method: Use the STOP-sequence and filtered-line probes to identify completion after SDA release with SCL high; sample registered cmd_ack after each posedge and assert a single-cycle high pulse aligned to that terminal phase, with low values on adjacent cycles.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=STOP with ena=1 and a released-high bus. While the STOP sequence is active, assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the SDA release terminal phase, then deassert nReset and clock several cycles without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Because the STOP sequence is aborted before its SDA release terminal phase, cmd_ack does not pulse at the canceled STOP terminal phase or during reset recovery (the 'otherwise' side of the requirement). The controller returns idle with both output enables released.
elements.check_method: Monitor the STOP-sequence probe and determine that the SDA release terminal phase was not reached; check cmd_ack asynchronously during reset and on every subsequent settled posedge for absence of a high pulse until a new valid command is issued.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, set ena=1, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) on an enabled timing tick, and provide a released-high SCL bus with the slave driving SDA data.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit phase, sda_oen is high: this is the holding side of shows, with SDA released for the slave to drive the data bit, and it remains released until the READ sequence completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the in_read_sequence probe to identify the READ data-bit phase and compare sampled sda_oen against 1 on every clock in that phase; assert that no sampled phase value is 0 before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, set ena=1 and din=0, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) on an enabled timing tick, and provide a released-high SCL bus.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is low: this is the contrasting otherwise side of shows, with the controller driving SDA instead of releasing it.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence probe to identify the WRITE data-bit phase and compare sampled sda_oen against 0 while din=0; record the complementary port behavior relative to the READ release case.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous and synchronous reset, release both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a finite value, then issue cmd=READ (1000) while the bus is idle and externally keep SDA high. Allow the READ command to reach its data-bit phase with SCL released high; keep the external SCL high through the sampling window.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during the READ sampling window, scl_oen remains 1, and after the sampling window completes the controller transitions scl_oen to 0 to drive SCL low again.
elements.check_method: Use the in_read_sequence probe and a reference model of clk_en, filtering, and READ phase progression to identify the sampling window. At every settled posedge, assert scl_oen==1 from release through the sampling window, then require exactly one subsequent registered transition to scl_oen==0 before READ completion/cmd_ack. Record bins for release, sustained-high window, and low transition.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous and synchronous reset, release both resets, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a finite value, issue cmd=READ (1000), and allow the controller to release SCL high for the READ sampling window. While the READ command is active and SCL is released, inject an unexpected filtered STOP by driving SDA from low to high while filtered SCL is high, causing arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: scl_oen does not exhibit the complete normal pattern of remaining 1 throughout the READ sampling window followed by a transition to 0; instead, arbitration loss aborts the active READ and the controller returns idle while releasing the bus, with no cmd_ack for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use stop_condition, fsm_active, and in_read_sequence probes to confirm the injected STOP occurs during READ. Compare scl_oen against the reference model: verify the normal READ low-phase transition is absent after the abort, both line enables are released, al becomes sticky, and cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command. Record bins for abort during released-high READ phase and missing normal scl_oen transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle. Model the external bus so the READ sequence releases SCL and the filtered SDA value is stable low before the filtered SCL rising edge in the sample window.
elements.expected_response: While in the READ sample window with scl_oen=1, when filtered SCL rises, dout updates on the corresponding registered clock edge to 0, the filtered SDA value at that edge.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-signal reference model to identify the READ sample-window filtered SCL rising edge; sample dout after the same posedge and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value. Record a bin for captured-zero.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle. Model the external bus so the READ sequence releases SCL and the filtered SDA value is stable high before the filtered SCL rising edge in the sample window.
elements.expected_response: While in the READ sample window with scl_oen=1, when filtered SCL rises, dout updates on the corresponding registered clock edge to 1, the filtered SDA value at that edge.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-signal reference model to identify the READ sample-window filtered SCL rising edge; sample dout after the same posedge and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value. Record a bin for captured-one.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ command and save the resulting dout value. Then, while the FSM is idle or in a non-READ phase with scl_oen released, create a filtered SCL rising edge while keeping the filtered SDA value different from the saved dout.
elements.expected_response: Because the READ SCL sample window is not active, dout does not update to the filtered SDA value corresponding to this rising edge; it retains its previously captured value.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_read_sequence, scl_oen, filtered_scl_rising, and dout. On a filtered SCL rising edge with in_read_sequence=0 or outside the READ sample window, compare dout after the posedge against its pre-edge value and require no update to the current filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a released-high bus, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000). Allow the READ sequence to proceed, provide the final sampled data bit, and drive a filtered SCL rising edge so the final bit is captured into dout.
elements.expected_response: After the final READ data-bit cycle completes and the command enters its terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock. This is the holding side of the requirement's shows statement: cmd_ack asserts to end the READ command.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify the final filtered SCL rising edge and terminal phase; compare dout with the bus SDA value at that edge, then assert that cmd_ack is high on the following registered terminal-completion observation and low on the next clock.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and cmd=READ active, inject an unexpected filtered STOP condition before the final READ data-bit cycle completes by transitioning filtered SDA from low to high while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: The active READ command aborts through arbitration loss, and cmd_ack does not assert in the would-be READ terminal phase. This is the contrasting side of the requirement's shows statement: cmd_ack does not assert when the final READ cycle does not complete.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered STOP event and al, then verify that the READ FSM returns to idle, both output enables are released, and no cmd_ack pulse occurs from the aborted command during the remaining terminal-phase observation window.

elements.stimulus: Run the requirement-to-testplan traceability audit for specification item 14; apply no command or bus stimulus to the DUT.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output value, timing, or state transition is required by REQ-0088.
elements.check_method: Review the traceability record and confirm that REQ-0088 is covered while no DUT assertion is generated for an unspecified obligation.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=4 (WRITE), set din=0, and provide a normal bus with filtered SCL able to rise and filtered SDA low during the released high phase. Hold inputs until the WRITE bit completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=0 side of the observed sda_oen behavior: during SDA setup and the released-SCL high phase, sda_oen=0, driving SDA low. During that high phase scl_oen=1 and sda_arbitration_check=1. After the high phase, scl_oen becomes 0 for the following low phase, and no arbitration loss is caused by SDA being low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard keyed to in_write_sequence and the high-phase probe. Compare registered sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge against the expected sequence, require sda_arbitration_check only during the released high phase, and assert that al and cmd_ack remain consistent with a normally completing WRITE.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, drive cmd=4 (WRITE), set din=1, and provide a normal bus with filtered SCL able to rise and filtered SDA high during the released high phase. Hold inputs until the WRITE bit completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=1 side of the observed sda_oen behavior: during SDA setup and the released-SCL high phase, sda_oen=1, releasing SDA. During that high phase scl_oen=1 and sda_arbitration_check=1. After the high phase, scl_oen becomes 0 for the following low phase, with no arbitration loss while filtered SDA remains high.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard keyed to in_write_sequence and the high-phase probe. Compare registered sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge against the expected sequence, require sda_arbitration_check only during the released high phase, and assert that al is not set and the WRITE proceeds to its normal completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and wait for in_idle. Present cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0 while the bus is released and SCL is allowed to reach high; maintain normal bus conditions through the complete WRITE sequence.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the WRITE sequence completes and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock during the terminal WRITE phase, then returns low while the command FSM returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_write_sequence, in_idle, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples. Assert that exactly one cmd_ack rising interval occurs after WRITE acceptance and before return to idle, that its width is one clock, and that no additional pulse follows.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and wait for in_idle. Present cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1. During the released-high SDA phase of the active WRITE sequence, externally pull SDA low while allowing SCL high so arbitration is lost; maintain the condition until the controller aborts.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast: the WRITE command aborts on arbitration loss and cmd_ack does not pulse at the end of the sequence; al asserts and the controller returns idle with both output enables released.
