elements.check_method: Detect the active WRITE phase and injected SDA-low condition, then monitor al, in_idle, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples. Assert that al becomes high, the FSM returns to idle without any cmd_ack high interval for this command, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.

elements.stimulus: Review list-item 15 and perform requirements-to-testplan traceability analysis; do not drive any DUT input based solely on REQ-0091.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavioral response, interface value, state transition, timing constraint, or protocol obligation is expected from REQ-0091.
elements.check_method: Static review confirms the requirement text and normalized expectation state that no requirement applies and that no DUT-observable behavior is specified; confirm the traceability record contains no inferred behavioral assertion.

elements.stimulus: Start with nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and the bus released. Assert nReset=0 between clk rising edges while providing arbitrary cmd, clk_cnt, din, scl_i, and sda_i values; hold nReset low across at least one clock edge.
elements.expected_response: At the asynchronous assertion of nReset, the reset-holding side of the observed behavior is present: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, in_idle=1, and filtered_scl_high=1. Counter and filter state are reset, with filtered SDA also initialized high.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous monitor at the nReset transition for the registered outputs and sample the probes after the following clock edge; compare against the reset reference model, including idle FSM state and initialized high filter values.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and the bus released, issue START and allow the controller to enter an active command phase. Then drive rst=1 before a clk rising edge and hold it high through that next rising edge, with arbitrary command and bus inputs.
elements.expected_response: On the next rising edge, the synchronous-reset side of the observed behavior is present: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, busy=0, in_idle=1, and filtered_scl_high=1. Counter and filter state are reset, with filtered SDA also initialized high. No active command phase remains after the reset edge.
elements.check_method: Sample all listed outputs and probes after nonblocking assignments settle on the first rising edge with rst=1, and compare them with the asynchronous-reset reference state; verify that the pre-reset active state has been replaced.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset=1 and rst=0, initialize the bus released-high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a valid START command, and provide clock edges until the START sequence is active and advances through its SDA-low and SCL-low phases.
elements.expected_response: The non-reset contrasting side of the observed behavior is present: while the command is active, in_idle=0 and the output enables reflect the START sequence rather than reset values—sda_oen becomes 0 during the SDA-low phase and scl_oen subsequently becomes 0 during the SCL-low phase. This demonstrates that scl_oen and sda_oen are not inherently held high, and in_idle is not inherently asserted, when reset does not hold.
elements.check_method: Use the FSM and timing reference model with clk_cnt=0 to predict each enabled phase; compare registered scl_oen and sda_oen after each rising edge and correlate them with in_start_sequence and in_idle probes.

elements.stimulus: Review the i2c_master_bit_ctrl specification and implementation documentation for the section headed "Processing Flow:".
elements.expected_response: A processing-flow description is present for the i2c_master_bit_ctrl module.
elements.check_method: Static document/artifact check that locates the exact "Processing Flow:" section and confirms it contains a processing-flow description for the module; no DUT output comparison is applicable.

elements.stimulus: At the beginning of a run, assert nReset low asynchronously between clock edges, then deassert it. Before issuing any command, verify the module is idle; then drive a valid command with ena high and wait for command acceptance.
elements.expected_response: The reset-initialized side of REQ-0094 applies: scl_oen is high after reset and remains established in the released idle state before normal command processing begins; subsequent processing starts only after this reset state has been established.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen asynchronously after nReset assertion and at each posedge after deassertion. Assert scl_oen == 1 before the first accepted command, and correlate command acceptance with in_idle and clk_en_asserted.

elements.stimulus: Start a fresh DUT run without asserting either reset input, leave nReset high and rst low, and attempt to issue a valid command with ena high on a clock-enable opportunity. Observe scl_oen before and when the first processing attempt occurs.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, non-holding side of REQ-0094 applies: processing begins without the reset-initialized output state being established first, so scl_oen is not required to be the reset-initialized high value and may remain unknown or retain a previously active low-drive value when the first command is processed.
elements.check_method: Use four-state observation of scl_oen before the first command-processing opportunity and compare it against the reset-case trace. Flag the reset-ordering violation if processing is accepted while scl_oen has not first been observed high as the reset-initialized state.

elements.stimulus: Hold rst low and nReset high, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt=0, wait until the command FSM is active, then drive nReset low between clock edges.
elements.expected_response: Asynchronous reset takes effect without waiting for clk: the module returns to idle, cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. These are the reset-state values described by the 'when reset holds' side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Assert sampled-after-delta-cycle checks immediately when nReset falls, without requiring a posedge clk; verify the listed output values and in_idle, and verify that no command-completion pulse is produced for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and rst low, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt=0, and observe the active START sequence without asserting either reset input.
elements.expected_response: The ordinary non-reset behavior is observed rather than the reset-state side: the FSM leaves idle and, during the START sequence, pulls SDA low so sda_oen=0; reset does not force cmd_ack, busy, al, scl_oen, and sda_oen to the reset tuple.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence probe and compare registered outputs after each posedge against the START reference model; specifically require an active START phase with sda_oen=0, contrasting with reset's required sda_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: Hold nReset high, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt=0, wait until the command FSM is active, then drive rst high before a rising edge and keep it high through that rising edge.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge with rst=1, synchronous reset returns the module to idle: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. These are the reset-state values described by the 'when reset holds' side of the observed port behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs after nonblocking assignments settle on the first posedge with rst high; verify the listed values and in_idle, and verify that the active command is aborted without a completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and rst low, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt=0, and observe the active START sequence without asserting either reset input.
elements.expected_response: The ordinary non-reset behavior is observed rather than the reset-state side: the FSM leaves idle and, during the START sequence, pulls SDA low so sda_oen=0; reset does not force the output ports to cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1 throughout command execution.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence probe and compare outputs after each posedge against the START reference model; require an active START phase with sda_oen=0, contrasting with synchronous reset's required sda_oen=1 after its reset edge.

elements.stimulus: Start from an active or non-idle transaction state with ena=1, then assert nReset=0 between clk rising edges while holding rst=0. Keep cmd, clk_cnt, din, scl_i, and sda_i stable.
elements.expected_response: Immediately upon asynchronous nReset assertion, the command FSM returns to idle; cmd_ack, busy, and al clear to 0; scl_oen and sda_oen become released high at 1; arbitration checking is disabled; counters and filtered-line state are reset or reloaded to the reset condition, with filtered SCL and SDA initialized high. This is the reset side of the specified port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous-reset assertion monitor to sample outputs without waiting for a clk edge, assert cmd_ack==0, busy==0, al==0, scl_oen==1, and sda_oen==1, and compare the idle/probe and internal reference-model reset state against the expected initialized state.

elements.stimulus: After allowing the DUT to leave reset and reach a non-reset state, assert rst=1 before a rising edge while nReset=1, and hold rst=1 across that rising edge. Keep ena=1 and all command and bus inputs stable.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge with synchronous rst asserted, the command FSM returns to idle; cmd_ack, busy, and al clear to 0; scl_oen and sda_oen are 1; arbitration checking is disabled; counters and filter state are reset or reloaded; and filtered SCL and SDA return to the idle-high initialized state. This is the reset side of the specified port behavior for synchronous reset.
elements.check_method: At the reset clock edge and after nonblocking updates settle, compare cmd_ack, busy, al, scl_oen, and sda_oen with the reset reference model, and verify the idle/probe and filtered-state model. Confirm no reset value is sampled before the synchronous reset edge.

elements.stimulus: With nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and the external bus released high, issue cmd=START while the FSM is idle. Continue clocking until the START sequence reaches its command-complete phase, then return cmd to NOP.
elements.expected_response: Outside reset initialization, the ports exhibit ordinary command behavior rather than remaining at reset values: the START sequence drives SDA low by making sda_oen=0 while SCL is high, subsequently drives SCL low by making scl_oen=0, and eventually produces one cmd_ack pulse. busy reflects the detected filtered START condition and may become 1; al remains 0 when no arbitration loss occurs. This is the non-reset side of the specified port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the variable-latency timing and filter reference model to identify START phases and completion. Assert the observed sequence of sda_oen and scl_oen, detect exactly one registered cmd_ack pulse, and compare busy/al against the expected filtered START and no-loss outcomes; specifically verify that at least one output-enable value differs from the reset release state during the command.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it high, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, and hold the external bus idle with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Then apply SDA/SCL input changes that are shorter than the filter interval or otherwise insufficient to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-valid-filtered-transition side of the observation: after reset busy remains low, or remains at its prior value, despite the input activity. No START indication is reflected at busy, demonstrating that post-reset SCL and SDA inputs continue to be sampled and filtered rather than being ignored.
elements.check_method: After reset release, sample busy on every posedge clk after registered updates settle. Confirm busy does not rise during the short or filtered-out input changes, and compare the observed result against a reference model of synchronization, filter sampling, and three-sample majority filtering.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, release it high, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to 0, and hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough to establish the filtered idle-high state. While SCL remains high, drive sda_i from 1 to 0 and hold both inputs stable for enough enabled clocks to pass synchronization and produce a valid filtered SDA falling transition.
elements.expected_response: This is the valid-sampled-transition side of the observation: busy rises on the registered cycle after the filtered START condition is processed. The change from busy low to busy high demonstrates that the module continuously samples the external SCL and SDA inputs after reset and uses the resulting filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage input synchronizers, filter sampling cadence, majority histories, and filtered edge detection. Check that the modeled START occurs with filtered SCL high and that busy asserts on the corresponding posedge with the specified one-cycle registered latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i high and sda_i high with ena high. Drive sda_i low and keep it low across enough rising edges of clk for the two-stage synchronizer and filter to settle, then observe busy.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0098: busy changes from 0 to 1 only after the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition is established while SCL is high. The change must not occur before the expected synchronizer and filter settling latency.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for cSDA/cSCL synchronization and the majority filter; compare the predicted filtered START detection and busy update cycle with the registered busy output sampled after each posedge.

elements.stimulus: With scl_i held high, sda_i initially high, and busy equal to 0, drive sda_i low only between two adjacent rising edges of clk and return it high before the next rising edge so the transition is too brief to be captured and propagated through the synchronizer and filter.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of REQ-0098: the raw SDA transition is not captured through the two-stage synchronizer and filter, no filtered START is detected, and busy remains at its prior value of 0.
elements.check_method: Ensure the injected pulse is absent at every sampling edge, run the synchronizer/filter reference model, and compare its unchanged busy prediction against the registered busy output for the full observation window.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, hold scl_i high and drive sda_i from high to low between clk rising edges to form a raw START candidate; continue holding the levels stable and run clk for the two capture stages plus the required filter-sampling and majority-detection window.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: busy remains low through the first two clk rising edges after the raw transition and changes to high only after the transition has propagated through the synchronized and filtered path used for START detection; it does not respond directly to the raw input transition.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, sample busy after registered updates settle. Assert busy is unchanged during the first two capture cycles, then compare the observed assertion cycle against a reference model of the two-stage synchronizer and filter pipeline; require the filtered START event to precede the busy assertion.

elements.stimulus: With busy high from a previously detected START, hold scl_i high and drive sda_i from low to high immediately before, at, and immediately after successive clk rising edges to form STOP candidates with different setup timing; keep the resulting bus levels stable long enough for synchronization and filtering.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise side of shows is prohibited: busy must not clear during the raw-transition edge or either of the first two clk capture edges, and must not vary with the raw transition's exact relationship to clk. It may clear only after the synchronized, filtered SDA rising transition is detected as a STOP.
elements.check_method: Run the three edge-placement variants and compare busy waveforms cycle-by-cycle to a two-stage-capture plus filter reference model. Flag any busy clear before the modeled synchronized/filter detection point or any clear whose timing depends on the raw input at the sampling edge.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a known nonzero value. After reset, drive sda_i low while keeping scl_i high and hold it long enough for synchronization and multiple filter sample ticks to accept the transition; then drive sda_i high and hold it similarly long enough for the reverse transition to be accepted.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of REQ-0109's observed behavior: busy rises after the filtered SDA high-to-low START transition is accepted while filtered SCL is high, and later falls after the filtered SDA low-to-high STOP transition is accepted. Neither busy transition occurs before the corresponding filtered transition is produced.
elements.check_method: Use the filter-sample tick and filtered transition reference model to predict acceptance cycles, then compare busy sampled after each posedge. Assert that busy changes only after the modeled filtered START or STOP transition and remains stable during the preceding synchronization/filtering interval.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, leaving busy at its reset value. Set ena=1. Drive sda_i low for less than the synchronization/filter acceptance window, then return it high before enough synchronized samples and filter sample ticks occur to establish a filtered SDA transition; repeat with a different short low pulse if needed.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of REQ-0109's observed behavior: the SDA glitch does not produce a filtered START or STOP, and busy remains at its prior value throughout the injection and afterward.
elements.check_method: Compare synchronized and filter-history state against a reference model to confirm that no filtered SDA high-to-low or low-to-high transition is generated, then assert that busy remains continuously equal to its pre-glitch value on every settled post-posedge sample.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; keep rst low, ena high, clk_cnt=16, scl_i high, and sda_i high until reset synchronization, filtering, and the two-stage input synchronizers have established a stable high bus. Then apply a stable sda_i high-to-low transition while scl_i remains high, and record enabled-clock intervals, filter sampling cadence, and the cycle on which busy rises.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0101: busy rises when the filtered START is detected, with filter samples occurring every floor(16 >> 2)=4 enabled clocks, apart from the synchronizer and three-sample majority-filter pipeline latency. The measured busy-detection latency must match the reference model using a four-enabled-clock filter sampling interval.
elements.check_method: Drive and sample on posedge clk after nonblocking updates. Compare the observed busy rising cycle and inferred sampling cadence against a reference model containing the two-stage synchronizers, filter counter reload, three-sample majority filter, and START edge detector; allow only the modeled pipeline latency.

elements.stimulus: Repeat reset and stable-bus initialization with ena high, then set clk_cnt=0. After the high bus is established, apply a stable sda_i high-to-low transition while scl_i remains high and record the enabled-clock interval and the cycle on which busy rises. Repeat with clk_cnt=3 as a small nonzero boundary value.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting boundary case: busy rises at the filtered START detection latency predicted for a sampling interval of max(1, floor(0 >> 2))=1 enabled clock for clk_cnt=0 and max(1, floor(3 >> 2))=1 enabled clock for clk_cnt=3. It must not exhibit a stuck filter counter, a zero-sample interval, or the latency expected from an unshifted clk_cnt value; such behavior is the 'otherwise' side of REQ-0101 and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: For each clk_cnt value, compare busy's observed rising cycle and inferred sample cadence with the reference model using max(1, floor(clk_cnt >> 2)); separately flag any interval of zero, raw clk_cnt, or a stalled counter as noncompliant.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16'd8, then drive stable SCL and SDA levels and apply input transitions. Run enough enabled clk cycles for the two-stage synchronizers and filter counter to expire multiple times.
elements.expected_response: When the filter counter expires and filter_sample_tick is asserted, the newly synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into the fSCL and fSDA three-sample histories. Between filter_sample_tick events, no new history sample is shifted. This is the 'requirement holds' side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the synchronizers, filter counter interval, and three-sample histories. Match each filter_sample_tick probe event to exactly one history shift and compare the resulting majority-filtered behavior and any resulting filtered edge indications against the DUT waveform.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=0 with clk_cnt=16'd8 and drive changing SCL and SDA input levels for several filter-counter intervals, then reassert ena=1 and continue running until a filter counter expiration occurs.
elements.expected_response: While ena=0, filter progression is disabled: filter_sample_tick does not assert and the fSCL and fSDA histories retain their prior values despite input changes. After ena returns high and the counter expires, filter_sample_tick asserts and the next synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted. This is the 'requirement does not hold' contrast.
elements.check_method: Check the filter_sample_tick probe and compare internal filter-history state or downstream majority-filtered outputs with a reference model. Require no history updates during the ena=0 interval, followed by one update per filter_sample_tick after re-enabling progression.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release both reset inputs, hold scl_i high and the external SDA line high, then set ena=1. After the filter histories are initialized high, drive sda_i low only long enough to produce one enabled filter sample tick, then return sda_i high before the next enabled filter sample tick. Allow synchronization and filtering to process the resulting three-sample SDA history while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case: the SDA history contains only one differing low sample, so the majority-filtered SDA remains high; no filtered SDA high-to-low transition occurs and busy remains unchanged low.
elements.check_method: At each filter_sample_tick, use a reference model of the synchronized three-sample SDA history and majority function, then compare the predicted absence of a filtered SDA transition with the registered busy output after the clock edge. Confirm busy never asserts.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release both reset inputs, hold scl_i high and the external SDA line high, then set ena=1. Drive sda_i low continuously across two consecutive enabled filter sample ticks, allowing synchronization and filtering to process each update while SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting transition case: when two of the three SDA history samples are low, majority logic changes filtered SDA from high to low; busy changes high after the filtered START transition is processed.
elements.check_method: At each filter_sample_tick, calculate the expected three-sample SDA majority with a reference model and identify the tick where it changes high-to-low. Compare busy after the corresponding posedge and require a registered transition from low to high, with no transition before the majority changes.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command with ena high and clk_cnt set to a value that permits multiple filter samples. During the READ data-bit phase, hold the external SDA line steadily at 1, release SCL, and drive SCL high long enough for synchronized samples to establish a majority-filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout updates to 1 on the posedge that processes the filtered SCL rising edge, demonstrating that the stable majority-filtered SDA value is used for READ capture rather than an unsynchronized raw input.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, three-sample histories, majority logic, and filtered-edge detection. At the modeled filtered SCL rising edge, compare the registered dout value after the posedge with the modeled majority-filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: During a READ data-bit phase, first establish dout at 0. Then apply SDA and SCL glitches shorter than the filter sampling interval, including SDA transitions that do not change the three-sample majority and SCL activity that does not produce a majority-filtered SCL rising edge. Keep the command active while these glitches occur.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: dout does not update in response to the raw or unstable SDA/SCL changes because they do not produce a filtered SCL rising edge or change the majority-filtered SDA value; it remains at its prior value of 0.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm that no qualifying filtered SCL rising edge or majority-filtered SDA transition occurs during the injected glitches, then assert that dout remains unchanged on every subsequent clock until a qualifying filtered capture event occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, operate the module with ena high and drive the synchronized bus inputs so the filtered SDA value is initially high and filtered SCL is high; then hold SCL high and apply a stable SDA high-to-low transition long enough for synchronization and filtering to update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed behavior: after the delayed filtered transition is registered, busy becomes 1. The transition must be reflected only after the reference-model delay for synchronization, majority filtering, and delayed filtered-signal detection; no raw-input transition may change busy earlier.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the synchronized inputs, three-sample filtered values, and delayed dSCL/dSDA values. Compare the predicted qualifying SDA falling transition with the registered busy output and assert that busy rises on the corresponding registered detection cycle.

elements.stimulus: Run two non-qualifying bus patterns with ena high: first hold filtered SDA unchanged while filtered SCL remains high; then drive a stable SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is low, allowing synchronization and filtering to settle in each case.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of the observed behavior: busy holds its prior value for the unchanged SDA case and also holds its prior value for the SDA transition occurring while filtered SCL is low. No busy transition is permitted from either pattern.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to verify that dSDA changes without a qualifying dSCL-high condition, or does not change at all, and compare busy cycle by cycle against its previous value; flag any busy change as a failure.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then keep ena high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for multiple filter sample ticks without issuing a START or STOP-producing command.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-difference side of the busy observation: busy retains its prior value, remaining 0, because the current filtered SCL/SDA values match their delayed values and do not indicate a START or STOP.
elements.check_method: At each filter_sample_tick, compare the reference model's current and delayed filtered values, and sample busy after the corresponding posedge; assert that busy remains 0 when no qualifying difference occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, present a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=START on an enabled clk_en tick, and allow the START sequence to pull SDA low while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the difference side of the busy observation: when the filtered SDA transition differs from its delayed value while filtered SCL is high, busy rises to 1 for the detected START.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of synchronization, majority filtering, and delayed-value comparison to identify the filtered SDA high-to-low transition; compare busy after the registered detection update and require a 0-to-1 transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while ena=1; keep SDA externally high throughout the released-high WRITE arbitration window and provide normal SCL high and low phases.
elements.expected_response: This is the no-difference side of the arbitration observation: al does not rise because the compared filtered SDA value does not indicate SDA low where a released high was expected; the WRITE completes with cmd_ack and al remains 0.
elements.check_method: During sda_arbitration_check, compare the reference model's current and delayed filtered SDA values and sample al and cmd_ack after each posedge; require no arbitration-loss indication and one normal completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while ena=1; during the released-high WRITE arbitration window, externally hold SDA low while the master releases it, then continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: This is the difference side of the arbitration observation: when filtered SDA differs from its delayed value so the comparison detects SDA low where high was expected, al rises and remains asserted, the active WRITE aborts, no cmd_ack is generated for that command, and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and delayed-value reference model to identify the qualifying filtered SDA difference during sda_arbitration_check; compare al, cmd_ack, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen after each posedge and require sticky al, no completion pulse, return to idle, and released lines.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive the bus released high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for synchronization and filter histories to settle. While keeping scl_i=1, drive sda_i=0 and hold both inputs stable long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition.
elements.expected_response: On the clock that processes the qualifying filtered transition, start_condition is asserted for the detected START condition. This is the holding side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronizer and majority-filter latency to identify the filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high; sample the start_condition probe after each posedge and require it to assert on the corresponding processing clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and establish filtered SCL low by driving scl_i=0. With sda_i initially high and filtered, drive sda_i=0 and hold it long enough for the filtered SDA high-to-low transition to occur while filtered SCL remains low; then return the bus to stable levels without creating a SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: start_condition remains deasserted for this non-qualifying transition. This is the non-holding side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that the filtered SDA transition occurs only while filtered SCL is low, then monitor start_condition after every posedge through filter settling and require no assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset deassertion, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive the released bus to filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low, wait until the reference synchronizer/filter model confirms those filtered values, then release SDA so the bus transitions from low to high while SCL remains high; hold both lines stable until the filtered transition is processed.
elements.expected_response: The controller asserts stop_condition for the valid STOP case: filtered SDA transitions low-to-high while filtered SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronization, filter-history, and majority model to identify the cycle of the filtered SDA rising transition with filtered SCL high; sample the stop_condition probe after each posedge and require it to assert on the corresponding processing cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset deassertion, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive the released bus to filtered SCL low and filtered SDA low, wait until the reference synchronizer/filter model confirms those filtered values, then release SDA so the bus transitions from low to high while SCL remains low; hold both lines stable through filter processing.
elements.expected_response: The controller does not assert stop_condition for the contrasting invalid case: the filtered SDA low-to-high transition occurs while filtered SCL is low.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to identify the filtered SDA rising transition and verify filtered SCL is low at that cycle; monitor stop_condition through the transition and subsequent settling window and require it to remain deasserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low, model the open-drain bus high, hold filtered SCL high, and drive SDA from filtered high to filtered low long enough for the synchronizer/filter reference model to detect a START condition. Keep the bus otherwise valid and sample busy after the resulting registered status update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0109: start_condition asserts for the filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high, and busy rises to 1 on the registered update immediately after the detected START.
elements.check_method: Compare the DUT busy output and start_condition probe against a reference model of synchronization, three-sample filtering, edge detection, and registered status update; require busy to transition 0-to-1 exactly after the modeled START detection.

elements.stimulus: First create a valid filtered START so busy is 1. Then hold filtered SCL high and drive SDA from filtered low to filtered high long enough for the synchronizer/filter reference model to detect a STOP condition. Keep the bus otherwise valid and sample busy after the resulting registered status update.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of REQ-0109: stop_condition asserts for the filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high, and busy falls to 0 on the registered update immediately after the detected STOP.
elements.check_method: Compare the DUT busy output and stop_condition probe against a reference model of synchronization, three-sample filtering, edge detection, and registered status update; require busy to transition 1-to-0 exactly after the modeled STOP detection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value. Issue a supported READ command while the external bus remains released and SCL follows the controller without being held low or falling unexpectedly while released.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting no-stretch/no-synchronization case: cmd_ack pulses at the normal READ command-completion point, without an additional wait or synchronized low-period delay.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for clk_en, filtering, and READ phase timing to predict the normal terminal phase; assert that cmd_ack is exactly one clock wide and occurs at the predicted completion point.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported READ command. When the controller releases SCL for the read window, externally hold SCL low for several enabled timing intervals, then release it high and allow the READ sequence to continue.
elements.expected_response: This is the clock-stretching holding case: cmd_ack is postponed until the stretched SCL timing window has completed, the controller observes released-high filtered SCL, resumes the command, and reaches its normal terminal phase; no early cmd_ack occurs while the stretched SCL remains low.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, filtered SCL, the slave_wait_active probe, and cmd_ack. Compare against a reference model that pauses the timing counter and FSM during slave wait; assert no cmd_ack before filtered SCL becomes high and assert one completion pulse after resumption.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a supported READ command. During the released-SCL phase, let SCL become high and then drive an external falling SCL edge while the controller still has SCL released; subsequently allow SCL to return high and let the command continue.
elements.expected_response: This is the multi-master synchronization holding case: the external falling edge causes a synchronized low-period delay and timing restart, so cmd_ack is postponed until the synchronized SCL-low interval has completed and the READ command resumes; no early cmd_ack occurs during that delay.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, scl_sync_active, filtered SCL edges, timing-counter/clk_en probes, and cmd_ack. Compare with a reference model that reloads the timing counter on the released-SCL falling edge; assert the added delay and exactly one cmd_ack at the resumed command-completion point.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and model the bus so that after the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), scl_i remains low long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to make filtered SCL low.
elements.expected_response: While scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait_active is asserted; the timing counter remains paused and the active command does not advance until filtered SCL becomes high or SCL is driven low by the controller.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the interval where scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL=0, then assert slave_wait_active=1 throughout that interval and verify no command-phase or timing-counter advancement occurs.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0, and model the external bus so scl_i is high early enough that, when the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1), the synchronized three-sample filter reports filtered SCL high.
elements.expected_response: When scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is high, the contrasting non-wait case applies: slave_wait_active remains deasserted, the timing counter is allowed to run, and the command proceeds through its next legal phase.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to locate the released-SCL interval with filtered SCL=1; compare the slave_wait_active probe against 0 and verify the FSM advances on subsequent clk_en ticks rather than remaining paused.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a supported command active, issue START followed by WRITE with din=0. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), externally hold scl_i low long enough for filtered SCL to remain low.
elements.expected_response: The requirement holds: slave_wait_active asserts while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL remains low, indicating that the slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low. The timing counter and active command phase remain paused until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: Use the slave_wait_active probe and a reference timing/FSM model. Assert that the probe becomes active only after released SCL is observed low through the filter, that clk_en and command-phase progression are suppressed during the wait, and that progression resumes after filtered SCL becomes high.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same ena=1 START-then-WRITE sequence with din=0, but when the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), allow scl_i to remain high so filtered SCL becomes high without clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: The requirement does not hold: slave_wait_active remains deasserted because the released SCL is not being held low. The timing counter generates clk_en normally and the active command advances through its high phase.
elements.check_method: Compare the slave_wait_active probe and FSM/timing probes against the no-stretch reference model. Verify that slave_wait_active stays low while scl_oen=1 and filtered SCL is high, and that clk_en and legal command-state transitions continue.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and wait until the active WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1). Then externally hold SCL low so filtered SCL remains low and slave_wait_active remains 1 for multiple enabled timing intervals.
elements.expected_response: While slave_wait_active is 1, the timing counter remains paused, clk_en_asserted does not occur, the bit-level FSM remains in the same active WRITE phase, and cmd_ack remains low with no command-complete pulse. This is the holding-case side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, assert that slave_wait_active remains 1, the active FSM phase probe does not change, timing_counter_expired and clk_en_asserted do not assert, and cmd_ack is 0 throughout the hold interval; use a cycle scoreboard to compare successive probe and output samples.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and the same nonzero clk_cnt, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and allow the released SCL line to remain externally high so filtered SCL becomes high and slave_wait_active clears during the active command.
elements.expected_response: After slave_wait_active transitions to 0, the timing counter resumes, the bit-level FSM advances through the remaining WRITE phases, and cmd_ack becomes a one-clock pulse when the command completes. This is the non-holding-case side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor slave_wait_active, clk_en_asserted, the active FSM phase probe, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples; require FSM progress and subsequent timing ticks only after slave_wait_active clears, and require exactly one cmd_ack pulse at terminal completion.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, ena high, and a valid prescaler, issue a READ command. Wait until the READ sequence has released SCL (scl_oen=1) and the shared SCL line is high, then externally drive scl_i from high to low and keep it low for at least the synchronization/filter observation interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the filtered external SCL falling edge is recognized while scl_oen remains 1, scl_sync_active asserts. The timing counter is reloaded and local low-period timing follows the shared-bus falling edge; the READ bit-level timing does not proceed as though the master-controlled SCL high phase had completed.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_sync_active and the READ phase timing with a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, filtering, divider reload, and FSM progression. Bin the falling-edge-held condition and compare the observed synchronization indication and subsequent phase timing against the model.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, prescaler, READ-command, and released-SCL setup, but keep scl_i high while scl_oen=1 for the corresponding observation interval; do not introduce an external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast case: scl_sync_active remains deasserted, no external-fall synchronization or timing-counter reload is triggered, and local timing follows the ordinary divider-driven released-SCL behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate reference model and compare this trace with TP-0000. Assert that scl_sync_active has no pulse and that no synchronization-induced timing change occurs in the no-fall interval; bin the no-fall condition separately.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, choose clk_cnt=4, keep filtered SCL high whenever SCL is released, and issue a START command. Record clk, scl_oen, cmd_ack, and the timing-counter reference-model state through the complete START sequence.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observation: successive scl_oen phase transitions in the START sequence, including command completion, occur only on enabled timing boundaries produced by cnt after loading from clk_cnt=4 and decrementing to expiration. The FSM remains in each phase between those boundaries, and cmd_ack occurs only after the terminal timed phase.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model that reloads cnt from clk_cnt and decrements it on each enabled clock. Compare every observed scl_oen transition and cmd_ack cycle against predicted counter-expiration ticks; assert no phase transition occurs before the predicted tick and that the inter-transition spacing matches the model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, choose clk_cnt=8, keep filtered SCL high whenever SCL is released, and issue a START command. Sample scl_oen on every posedge, especially on clocks between successive predicted cnt expirations.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding side of the observation: scl_oen must not advance on clocks that do not satisfy the clk_cnt-governed timing interval. It must hold its current phase between counter boundaries; an unconstrained or fixed-cycle phase progression independent of clk_cnt is a failure.
elements.check_method: Build the expected cnt schedule from clk_cnt=8 and compare the sampled scl_oen sequence cycle by cycle. Check that all phase transitions align with predicted expiration ticks and that changing the prescale value from the smaller-value reference run changes phase spacing consistently rather than allowing transitions at the same unconstrained cycles.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=4, provide a released-high bus, issue a START command on a rising edge, then keep cmd at NOP and maintain scl_i and sda_i high without clock stretching or synchronization events.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: during the active START sequence, scl_oen remains in each SCL phase while the internal counter decrements and changes phase only at the clk_cnt-derived timing-enable tick. The measured interval from each counter reload to the corresponding scl_oen phase transition matches the reference model for clk_cnt=4; no transition occurs earlier than the prescribed interval.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model that loads the timing counter from clk_cnt and decrements it on every posedge clk. Record scl_oen after each settled posedge, correlate each phase transition with the model's counter-expiration tick, and assert that all START phase transitions match the predicted cycle.

elements.stimulus: Run two otherwise identical START transactions with ena=1 and a released-high bus: first set clk_cnt=1, then set clk_cnt=8, issue START, and keep cmd at NOP with scl_i and sda_i high and no slave wait or synchronization event. Measure scl_oen phase-transition cycles from command acceptance in both runs.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observed behavior: scl_oen transitions in the clk_cnt=8 run occur later and with the longer counter-derived phase intervals than in the clk_cnt=1 run. If the counter were not loaded from clk_cnt or were not decremented on each rising edge, the two runs would show identical or otherwise non-modelled transition timing; such behavior is a failure. Both runs must match their respective reference-model schedules.
elements.check_method: Compare the recorded scl_oen transition cycle numbers from both transactions against independent reference-model traces. Assert that the clk_cnt=8 schedule has the expected larger intervals and that neither schedule is invariant to the changed clk_cnt value.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, then issue a valid START command while monitoring the timing counter and clk_en_asserted. Allow the enabled counter to decrement through its programmed interval until the reference model identifies counter expiry.
elements.expected_response: When the timing counter expires, clk_en_asserted is asserted for the expiry clock and the command FSM advances from its current START timing phase on that timing enable. This is the holding side of the required observation difference: the timing counter has expired and clk_en is asserted.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider model seeded with clk_cnt=3 to predict the expiry cycle; compare the predicted expiry indication with clk_en_asserted and verify the FSM phase/probe changes only on that cycle.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, deassert reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3, issue a valid START command, and observe the clocks during the interval after the counter is loaded but before the reference model predicts expiry.
elements.expected_response: On every enabled clock for which the timing counter has not expired, clk_en_asserted remains deasserted and the command FSM does not advance due to a timing enable. This is the contrasting side of the required observation difference: the timing counter has not expired and clk_en is not asserted.
elements.check_method: Compare each pre-expiry cycle against the reference counter model; assert that clk_en_asserted=0 and that the command FSM timing state is unchanged on those cycles.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, provide a released-high bus, then issue a valid START command. After the START sequence is active, run the divider until the reference model identifies a clk_en assertion at a bit-timing phase boundary.
elements.expected_response: This is the asserted side of shows: when clk_en is asserted, scl_oen changes on the following registered update to the value prescribed by the next START bit-timing phase, demonstrating that the command FSM advanced only on the timing-enable tick.
elements.check_method: At every active START phase boundary, compare the observed scl_oen transition and cycle against a reference divider/FSM model. Require the transition to coincide with the modeled clk_en tick, accounting for the one-clock registered scl_oen latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value large enough to create multiple enabled clock cycles between timing ticks, provide a released-high bus, issue a valid START command, and observe an active START phase during an interval in which the reference model says clk_en is not asserted.
elements.expected_response: This is the not-asserted side of shows: while clk_en is not asserted, scl_oen holds its current phase value on every intervening posedge and does not advance to the next START bit-timing phase; it changes only after the next modeled clk_en tick.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider to identify cycles without clk_en, sample scl_oen after each posedge, and require it to remain equal to its prior phase value throughout those cycles. Then confirm the subsequent phase change occurs only at the next modeled clk_en tick, with the specified one-clock output registration.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt to a small nonzero value, issue a supported START command with ena high, and then drive ena low once the START command has been accepted and remains active. Hold ena low for several timing-counter periods without asserting reset.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack remains low and no command-complete pulse occurs for the entire ena-low interval. The active command does not complete while disabled; after ena is driven high again, the command resumes and eventually produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every settled posedge while ena is low and assert that it never pulses; compare the post-reenable phase progression and eventual one-clock acknowledgment against a reference model that reloads the timing counter whenever ena is low.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt to the same small nonzero value, issue the same supported START command with ena held high throughout the active command, and provide a released-high bus so the command can complete normally.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting enabled side of the observed behavior: the command sequence progresses normally and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle at completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack and compare its eventual single-cycle completion pulse and command latency against the enabled reference-model timing; verify that completion occurs without any ena-induced stall.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) from idle with din=1, and allow the command to advance through the WRITE sequence without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: when the WRITE operation begins, scl_oen or sda_oen departs from the released idle pair, and during the released high phase of each WRITE bit sda_arbitration_check is asserted so SDA arbitration is performed.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_write_sequence, sda_arbitration_check, scl_oen, and sda_oen on each settled posedge. Confirm that the WRITE sequence is entered, the output-enable pair leaves the released idle state at sequence start, and sda_arbitration_check asserts during the WRITE released-high phase while sda_i remains high; verify the command completes with cmd_ack and no al.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus, then issue cmd=START (0001) from idle and allow the command to run without issuing a WRITE command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of shows: because the controller is not executing a WRITE operation, sda_arbitration_check remains deasserted and no WRITE-specific arbitration-check phase occurs; the output-enable pair follows the START sequence rather than the WRITE-sequence departure.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_write_sequence, sda_arbitration_check, scl_oen, and sda_oen on each settled posedge. Confirm in_write_sequence never asserts and sda_arbitration_check never asserts throughout the START operation, while output enables match the START sequence and cmd_ack occurs once.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=1, provide a released-high SCL bus, and run until the WRITE FSM reaches its stable high phase while the command is active.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the WRITE FSM is in its stable high phase, the sda_arbitration_check probe is asserted, indicating that the internal sda_chk control is enabled.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence and sda_arbitration_check probes sampled after each posedge; require sda_arbitration_check=1 during the stable-high WRITE phase identified by the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Execute the same enabled WRITE command with din=1 and a released-high SCL bus, and sample the transaction during the initial WRITE setup phase, the SCL-low phase, and after the WRITE command returns to idle, excluding the stable high phase.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: while the FSM is not in the stable high phase of a WRITE bit, sda_arbitration_check is deasserted; the arbitration-check control is enabled only for the specified stable-high phase.
elements.check_method: Correlate sda_arbitration_check with the reference-model phase and in_write_sequence probe on every clock; require sda_arbitration_check=0 for all sampled non-stable-high phases and after return to idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al=0, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=1, and use clk_cnt=0. Accept the command from idle with SCL initially high, allow the WRITE sequence to reach its stable high phase with sda_oen=1 and sda_arbitration_check=1, and externally hold SDA low so the synchronized three-sample filtered SDA value is low. Keep SCL high until the arbitration check is processed.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observed difference: while SDA is released high but filtered SDA is observed low during SDA arbitration checking, al asserts on the processing clock and the command is aborted without cmd_ack; the controller releases both output-enable lines.
elements.check_method: Use the sda_oen, sda_arbitration_check, and filtered_sda_low probes to qualify the check window; sample al and cmd_ack after each posedge following settled nonblocking updates. Compare against a reference model of synchronization and majority filtering, and require al to transition from 0 to 1 in the qualified window and no cmd_ack for the aborted WRITE.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al=0, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), din=1, and use clk_cnt=0. Accept the command from idle with SCL initially high, allow the WRITE sequence to reach its stable high phase with sda_oen=1 and sda_arbitration_check=1, and externally release SDA high so the synchronized three-sample filtered SDA value remains high throughout the arbitration check.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of the observed difference: when SDA is released high and filtered SDA is not observed low during SDA arbitration checking, al does not newly assert; the WRITE proceeds to its normal subsequent phase rather than being aborted for arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Use the sda_oen, sda_arbitration_check, and filtered_sda_low probes to qualify the stable-high check window; sample al and the WRITE-sequence probe after each posedge. Compare with the filtered-line reference model and require filtered_sda_low=0, al to remain 0, and normal WRITE progression with no arbitration-loss abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a small nonzero value. Issue a WRITE command with din=0, wait for the command to be accepted and the write FSM to become active, then drive the external bus so filtered SCL is high and filtered SDA transitions from low to high, producing a filtered STOP condition before the WRITE completes.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-detection event while the non-STOP command is active, al asserts and remains asserted; this is the holding case of the requirement. The aborted WRITE does not generate cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the fsm_active and stop_condition probes to identify the qualifying event, then sample al and cmd_ack after the following posedge. Require al to transition high and remain high until reset, and require no cmd_ack pulse for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a small nonzero value. Issue the STOP command while idle and allow its STOP sequence to execute with the bus initially released high; let the requested STOP sequence drive SDA low, release SCL, and then release SDA while filtered SCL is high so that a filtered STOP condition is detected during the active STOP command.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-detection event during the requested STOP command, al remains deasserted; this is the contrasting non-holding case because the current command is STOP. The STOP command completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the in_stop_sequence and stop_condition probes to identify the STOP-command detection event. Sample al and cmd_ack after each posedge, requiring al to remain 0 and cmd_ack to assert for exactly one clock at command completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a WRITE command with din=1 and ena high. Allow the command to reach its released-SDA high phase, then externally hold SDA low while SCL is high so the filtered SDA is low during the arbitration check.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed behavior: when arbitration loss becomes visible, al asserts, the FSM returns to idle, and both scl_oen and sda_oen become high and remain high in the resulting idle window, releasing SCL and SDA. No command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: At the clock edge processing the filtered arbitration-loss condition and on subsequent clocks, sample al, in_idle, scl_oen, and sda_oen after registered updates. Assert al=1, in_idle=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1; verify no cmd_ack pulse occurs after the abort.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a WRITE command with din=0 and ena high. During the released-SCL high phase, externally hold SDA low, allowing the filtered SDA to remain low through the high phase and then allowing the command to proceed to its SCL-low phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding contrast of the observed behavior: because din=0 expects SDA low, the low SDA observation does not cause arbitration loss. The FSM does not return to idle and does not produce the arbitration-loss response of both enables high; during the following WRITE low phase, in_idle=0 and both scl_oen and sda_oen are low to drive SCL and SDA low.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered WRITE high phase and the subsequent low phase. Confirm al remains 0, in_idle remains 0, and after the next valid timing tick scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0, demonstrating that the command continued instead of entering the idle state with both lines released.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a READ command (cmd=4'b1000) with ena=1 and allow the READ sequence to become active. Drive the filtered SDA reference value to 0, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge while in the READ sequence; repeat with filtered SDA equal to 1 on a subsequent filtered SCL rising edge before command completion.
elements.expected_response: For each filtered SCL rising edge while the READ sequence is active, dout updates on the following registered observation to the value of the filtered SDA line at that sampling event: first 0, then 1. This is the holding side of observed_via.shows: dout updates to the value of filtered SDA.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for synchronization, three-sample majority filtering, and filtered SCL edge detection. At each modeled filtered SCL rising edge with in_read_sequence asserted, compare post-posedge dout with the modeled filtered SDA value captured for that edge, and verify the registered update occurs once per event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the command FSM idle or execute a non-READ command such as WRITE until in_read_sequence is deasserted. Change the filtered SDA value, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge while the READ sequence is inactive; repeat with a different filtered SDA value on another non-READ filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: On each filtered SCL rising edge when the READ sequence is inactive, dout does not update from the filtered SDA value for that event; it retains its prior value. This is the contrasting side of observed_via.shows: dout does not update to the value of filtered SDA.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and edge reference model to identify filtered SCL rising edges while in_read_sequence is 0. Compare dout before and after each corresponding posedge and require that it remains unchanged despite the modeled filtered SDA value changing.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1, issue a READ command on an enabled timing tick, and drive the external bus so filtering produces filtered SCL low followed by a rising edge while filtered SDA is stable at 1. Continue enabled filter progression through the rising edge.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: when the filtered_scl_rising probe is asserted, dout updates on the following registered observation to 1, the filtered SDA value at that rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the exact filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value; sample dout after the corresponding posedge and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: After reset and with ena=1, complete a filtered SCL rising edge with filtered SDA=0 to establish dout=0, then during an enabled READ operation change the external SDA so its filtered value changes to 1 while keeping filtered SCL low; do not produce a subsequent filtered SCL rising edge during the observation window.
elements.expected_response: NON-HOLDING CASE: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs after filtered SDA changes, dout does not capture the new filtered SDA value and remains 0.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model and filtered_scl_rising probe to confirm that no filtered SCL rising edge occurs after the SDA change; compare dout before and after the interval and require no update to 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, assert ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled timing tick. During the active READ sequence, release SDA and drive the external bus so the filtered SDA value is 0 when a filtered SCL rising edge occurs; keep the READ active until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: On the registered update following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout becomes 0 and carries the filtered SDA bit captured for use as the received data bit. This is the holding side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, majority filtering, filtered SCL edge detection, and READ sequencing; at each filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack compare dout after the posedge update with the model's filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, assert ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled timing tick. During the active READ sequence, release SDA and drive the external bus so the filtered SDA value is 1 when a filtered SCL rising edge occurs; keep the READ active until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: On the registered update following the filtered SCL rising edge, dout becomes 1 and carries the filtered SDA bit captured for use as the received data bit. This is the holding side of the requirement's shows condition for the opposite data value.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, majority filtering, filtered SCL edge detection, and READ sequencing; at each filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack compare dout after the posedge update with the model's filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, leave ena=1, keep the command FSM idle with cmd=NOP, and drive a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is 1. Do not issue a READ command or enter the READ sequence.
elements.expected_response: dout does not update to 1 as a received READ data bit on this filtered SCL rising edge; it retains its previously registered value. This is the contrasting, non-holding side of the requirement's shows condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_read_sequence and the reference filter model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge while READ is inactive, then compare dout before and after the registered update and confirm it does not equal the current filtered SDA solely because of that edge.

elements.stimulus: Apply and release reset so the FSM is idle. Set ena=1, cmd=START (4'b0001), and clk_cnt to a value large enough that clk_en will not assert for several enabled clocks. Hold these inputs stable and run clocks before the timing counter expires.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement's observation difference: in_idle remains asserted for every clock before clk_en_asserted; the valid command does not advance the FSM early.
elements.check_method: Sample the in_idle probe after each posedge and assert it remains 1 until the reference divider model predicts timing_counter_expired and clk_en_asserted. Record a coverage bin for valid command presented while idle and waiting for clk_en.

elements.stimulus: Apply and release reset so the FSM is idle. Set ena=1, cmd=START (4'b0001), and a known clk_cnt value. Hold the command and enable active until the reference divider reaches expiration and clk_en_asserted occurs.
elements.expected_response: Advancing side of the requirement's observation difference: on the enabled timing event, the FSM leaves idle and enters the START sequence, so in_idle deasserts and in_start_sequence asserts after the corresponding registered update.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider to predict clk_en_asserted, then compare the post-posedge in_idle and in_start_sequence probes. Assert that in_idle is 1 before the tick and becomes 0 on the first permitted FSM advance.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus released high, drive ena=1, hold cmd=START (4'b0001), and wait for an enabled clk_en acceptance tick while the command FSM is idle.
elements.expected_response: The START command is decoded: sda_oen initially remains released, then becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1, followed by the remainder of the START sequence and one cmd_ack pulse. This is the holding side of the START shows clause.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_start_sequence, sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack at settled posedge clk samples; compare the observed ordered signature against the START reference sequence and require exactly one acknowledgement pulse.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction with a valid START, then while the command FSM is idle between transactions drive ena=1, hold cmd=STOP (4'b0010), and wait for an enabled clk_en acceptance tick.
elements.expected_response: The STOP command is decoded: sda_oen becomes 0 before SCL is released, then sda_oen becomes 1 while scl_oen remains 1, followed by one cmd_ack pulse. This is the holding side of the STOP shows clause.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_stop_sequence, sda_oen, scl_oen, busy, and cmd_ack; verify the ordered STOP output-enable transitions, completion, and exactly one acknowledgement pulse.

elements.stimulus: While the command FSM is idle, drive ena=1 and cmd=READ (4'b1000), wait for an enabled clk_en acceptance tick, and provide a released-high SCL with the external device returning a stable SDA data bit and completing the read clock phase.
elements.expected_response: The READ command is decoded and enters the READ sequence; sda_oen remains 1 during the data-bit phase, allowing the external slave to drive SDA, and the command eventually produces one cmd_ack pulse. This is the holding side of the READ shows clause.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_read_sequence, sda_oen, filtered_scl_rising, dout, and cmd_ack; verify SDA remains released through the read window, data is captured on filtered SCL rising, and exactly one acknowledgement follows completion.

elements.stimulus: While the command FSM is idle, drive ena=1, din=0, and cmd=WRITE (4'b0100); wait for an enabled clk_en acceptance tick and provide a normal released-high SCL phase with filtered SDA low.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE command is decoded and enters the WRITE data phase; sda_oen becomes 0 for din=0, the write completes normally, and one cmd_ack pulse is produced without arbitration loss. This is the holding side of the WRITE shows clause for din=0.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_write_sequence, sda_oen, scl_oen, sda_arbitration_check, al, and cmd_ack; compare sda_oen with din, verify ordered SCL phases, and require completion without al and with exactly one ack.

elements.stimulus: While the command FSM is idle, drive ena=1, din=1, and cmd=WRITE (4'b0100); wait for an enabled clk_en acceptance tick and keep filtered SDA high during the released-high write phase.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE command is decoded and enters the WRITE data phase; sda_oen becomes 1 for din=1, arbitration checking is enabled during the released high phase, and the write completes with one cmd_ack and no arbitration loss. This is the holding side of the WRITE shows clause for din=1.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, in_write_sequence, sda_oen, sda_arbitration_check, al, and cmd_ack; verify sda_oen follows din, arbitration checking occurs only in the released-high phase, and completion has exactly one ack with al low.

elements.stimulus: While the command FSM is idle, drive ena=1 and cmd first to NOP (4'b0000), then repeat with an unsupported encoding such as 4'b0011; provide enabled clk_en ticks for both trials.
elements.expected_response: Neither value is decoded as an executable command: the FSM remains idle, no command-specific SDA/SCL output-enable sequence occurs, and cmd_ack remains low. This is the contrasting side of the observed shows clauses.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, all command-sequence probes, sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack across both trials; require no transition into an active sequence, no output-enable command signature, and no cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset and release it with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. After observing in_idle=1, drive cmd=4'b0001 (START) and hold it through the next enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The recognized START command moves the FSM from idle into the START command sequence; in_start_sequence becomes 1 and in_idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At the first clk_en_asserted tick after cmd is presented, sample the FSM probes after the posedge and assert in_start_sequence=1 and in_idle=0.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset and release it with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. After observing in_idle=1, drive cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) and hold it through the next enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The recognized STOP command moves the FSM from idle into the STOP command sequence; in_stop_sequence becomes 1 and in_idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At the first clk_en_asserted tick after cmd is presented, sample the FSM probes after the posedge and assert in_stop_sequence=1 and in_idle=0.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset and release it with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. After observing in_idle=1, drive cmd=4'b1000 (READ) and hold it through the next enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The recognized READ command moves the FSM from idle into the READ command sequence; in_read_sequence becomes 1 and in_idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At the first clk_en_asserted tick after cmd is presented, sample the FSM probes after the posedge and assert in_read_sequence=1 and in_idle=0.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset and release it with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. After observing in_idle=1, drive cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE), set din=0, and hold cmd through the next enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The recognized WRITE command moves the FSM from idle into the WRITE command sequence; in_write_sequence becomes 1 and in_idle becomes 0. This is the recognized-command side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At the first clk_en_asserted tick after cmd is presented, sample the FSM probes after the posedge and assert in_write_sequence=1 and in_idle=0.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset and release it with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. While in_idle=1, present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP), then repeat from idle with each unsupported value in {4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, 4'b1111}, holding each value through an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: For NOP and every unsupported command value, the FSM remains in idle: in_idle stays 1 and none of in_start_sequence, in_stop_sequence, in_read_sequence, or in_write_sequence becomes 1. This is the unsupported-or-idle side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: At each clk_en_asserted tick while each command value is presented, sample the FSM probes after the posedge and assert in_idle=1 and all four command-sequence probes=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold the bus externally high with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue cmd=START (4'b0001), and keep the command asserted until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after command acceptance, scl_oen and sda_oen are initially released high; sda_oen then changes low while scl_oen remains high, creating SDA low while SCL is released high; subsequently scl_oen changes low for the SCL-low phase. The phase ordering is preserved until the one-clock cmd_ack completion pulse.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, use a waveform assertion or reference-model comparison to verify the ordered sequence scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, followed by scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=0, followed by scl_oen=0; require no ordering inversion and correlate completion with exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue cmd=NOP (4'b0000) while the FSM is idle, and maintain NOP for multiple enabled timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: the controller does not enter the START sequence, so sda_oen does not transition from released high to driven low while scl_oen remains high, scl_oen does not transition into the START sequence's SCL-low phase, and no cmd_ack pulse is generated; both output enables remain released high.
elements.check_method: Monitor in_idle, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples across several clk_en ticks; assert that in_idle remains asserted, both output enables remain high, and the START-specific ordered transition is absent.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, drive a released-high bus with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then issue cmd=4'b0001 (START). Allow the filtered START condition to be generated and continue supplying enabled timing ticks until the START terminal phase completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the START condition, scl_oen becomes low to pull SCL low, in_idle becomes asserted on the command-completion edge, and cmd_ack becomes high for exactly one clock cycle before returning low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard/reference model of the START FSM sequence and clk_en timing. At each posedge after registered outputs settle, assert the expected scl_oen and in_idle values at completion, detect a cmd_ack rising edge at that edge, and assert cmd_ack is low on the immediately following clock and throughout the remainder of the transaction.

elements.stimulus: With nReset released, rst=0, ena=1, and scl_i=sda_i=1, issue cmd=4'b0001 (START). After the filtered START condition is observed but before the next timing-enable tick that executes the terminal START phase, sample the DUT; then allow the sequence to continue only after this observation.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-completion case: before the terminal completion edge, scl_oen remains released high, cmd_ack remains low, and in_idle remains deasserted because the START command is still active.
