This is the ordinary behavior corresponding to the 'otherwise' side of the observed port shows, not command completion.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the interval between filtered START detection and the terminal START timing tick. Sample scl_oen, cmd_ack, and in_idle after each posedge in that interval; require scl_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, and in_idle=0, and ensure no completion pulse is reported before the terminal edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, ensure the bus is released with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and issue cmd=0010 (STOP) on an enabled timing tick. Continue clocking until the STOP command completes.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of shows is observed: sda_oen first becomes low, then scl_oen becomes high while sda_oen remains low, and finally sda_oen becomes high while scl_oen remains high. The sequence generates the STOP ordering before command completion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate assertion or scoreboard on registered output enables. Verify the ordered phase sequence sda_oen=0 -> scl_oen=1 with sda_oen=0 -> sda_oen=1 with scl_oen=1, and reject any SDA release before SCL release or any SCL reassertion before SDA release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, issue cmd=0010 (STOP) on an enabled timing tick, and externally hold scl_i=0 after the controller releases SCL. Keep the external SCL low long enough to span multiple clock and timing ticks, then release scl_i=1.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting otherwise side of shows must not occur: sda_oen must not be released high while SCL remains externally or filtered low. The controller may keep sda_oen low while waiting, but once SDA is released, scl_oen must already be high and must remain high.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen, sda_oen, scl_i, and the filtered SCL reference cycle by cycle. Assert that no transition sda_oen:0->1 occurs before filtered SCL is high and after scl_oen has become high; flag the otherwise condition if SDA is released while SCL is low or before SCL release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) on an enabled timing tick. Provide a released-high external SCL response so the STOP sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL, observes filtered SCL high, and then releases SDA.
elements.expected_response: At the terminal STOP release phase, the FSM returns to idle (in_idle=1) and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock; cmd_ack is low on the following clock. This is the holding case of the observed behavior: cmd_ack pulses when the FSM returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked scoreboard keyed to the STOP terminal phase: verify the registered output-enable ordering, sample in_idle and cmd_ack after each posedge, require cmd_ack=1 on the completion cycle and cmd_ack=0 on the next cycle, and require in_idle to remain asserted after completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=4'b0010 (STOP). Once the STOP sequence is active but before its terminal phase releases SDA with filtered SCL high, assert nReset=0 asynchronously, then release nReset without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: The reset aborts the in-progress STOP sequence and no cmd_ack pulse is produced at the aborted STOP's would-be completion point; after reset initialization the FSM is idle. This is the contrasting side of the observed behavior: otherwise cmd_ack does not pulse at STOP sequence completion.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every clock from STOP acceptance through the reset and the next several clocks; assert it never rises for the aborted command, and verify in_idle becomes asserted by reset initialization. Distinguish any later acknowledgment by requiring no new command is issued.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while the bus is released and SCL is high. Allow the READ command to advance through its setup phase; drive a valid external SCL high phase with the slave holding SDA at both 0 and 1 in separate iterations, then allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit phase, while the controller is executing the READ command and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is high. This is the shows side of the requirement: SDA is released so the external slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge clk, use the in_read_sequence probe and the reference FSM model to identify the READ data-bit phase, then assert sda_oen==1 throughout that phase and before cmd_ack. Confirm the external SDA value can be observed without DUT SDA drive contention.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) with din=0 while the bus is released. Allow the WRITE command to enter its data-bit phase and provide normal SCL timing until completion.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is low, driving SDA rather than releasing it. This is the otherwise side of the requirement's shows distinction: the port does not exhibit the READ-command release behavior outside the READ data-bit phase.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge clk, use the in_write_sequence probe and the reference FSM model to identify the WRITE data-bit phase, then assert sda_oen==0 during the phase and compare it against the READ-case expectation of sda_oen==1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while the FSM is idle, and keep the external SCL high throughout the read window.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during in_read_sequence, scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL for the READ read window, and at the end of that window it subsequently becomes 0 to pull SCL low again.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen and in_read_sequence after each posedge clk; use a temporal assertion that a READ sequence contains an interval with in_read_sequence=1 and scl_oen=1 followed by scl_oen=0 at the read-window completion transition, allowing for the registered one-clock output latency.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1; issue cmd=NOP (4'b0000) while the FSM is idle and do not issue a READ command.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case of shows: because no READ read-window phase is entered, scl_oen does not exhibit a READ-specific released-high-then-pulled-low sequence; it remains in the idle released state rather than transitioning through the READ window completion.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen and in_read_sequence after each posedge clk and assert that in_read_sequence remains 0 and no scl_oen=1-to-0 transition is associated with a READ read-window phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue a READ command, allow the controller to release SDA and SCL, drive the external SDA line to 0, and drive SCL from low to high long enough for the synchronizer/filter reference model to produce one filtered SCL rising edge during the READ data-bit capture window. Repeat a second READ data-bit capture with filtered SDA driven to 1.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING side of shows: on each filtered SCL rising edge in the READ capture window, dout becomes equal to the filtered SDA value sampled at that edge: 0 for the first bit and 1 for the second bit, with the registered update visible after the processing posedge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronization, three-sample majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. At every modeled filtered SCL rising edge while in_read_sequence is active, compare dout after the processing posedge with the modeled filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: Complete or begin a READ operation and establish dout=0 from a prior filtered SCL rising edge. While the controller is in the READ data-bit capture window, keep filtered SCL high without creating another filtered SCL rising edge, change the external SDA line from 0 to 1, and allow the filter to settle while ena remains high.
elements.expected_response: OTHERWISE side of shows: because no new filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not capture the changed filtered SDA value; it retains its prior value of 0 rather than becoming 1.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that filtered SCL has no rising edge during the SDA transition and settling interval, then assert that dout remains unchanged at 0 throughout that interval and is not updated until a subsequent modeled filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle, keep the external SDA value stable, allow the READ sequence to release SCL and reach a filtered SCL rising edge, then allow the following SCL-low phase and terminal READ bit-cycle processing to complete without reset or arbitration injection.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed cmd_ack behavior: after the READ bit cycle completes, the command FSM enters idle and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock; cmd_ack is low on the surrounding clocks.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, correlate the terminal READ phase and in_idle probe with cmd_ack. Require in_idle=1 and a single cmd_ack=1 pulse on the completion clock, with cmd_ack=0 on the preceding and following clocks.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000), wait until the READ FSM is active with SCL released high, then drive a filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL remains high before the normal READ bit cycle completes; do not assert either reset input.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observed cmd_ack behavior: because the READ is aborted rather than reaching normal read-bit-cycle completion, cmd_ack does not assert at the abort/completion opportunity; the normal one-clock READ completion acknowledgment is absent.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered STOP event and fsm_active/in_idle probes, then sample cmd_ack after every posedge through the abort. Flag any cmd_ack pulse associated with the aborted READ, and specifically require cmd_ack=0 at the cycle where a normal READ completion pulse would otherwise be observed.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, provide a normal bus with scl_i high and sda_i low, then issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0. Wait for the WRITE command to be accepted and observe through completion before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of shows: during the WRITE data phase after acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, so the active-low open-drain output drives SDA low. The WRITE proceeds without arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: At each clock while the in_write_sequence probe is asserted after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, compare sda_oen against 0 and verify al remains 0; record a coverage bin for the din=0 mapping.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, provide a normal bus with scl_i high and sda_i high, then issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1. Wait for the WRITE command to be accepted and observe through completion before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting side of shows: during the WRITE data phase after acceptance and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA high rather than driving it low. The WRITE proceeds without arbitration loss when sda_i remains high.
elements.check_method: At each clock while the in_write_sequence probe is asserted after command acceptance and before cmd_ack, compare sda_oen against 1 and verify al remains 0; record a coverage bin for the din=1 mapping.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and a supported clk_cnt, then issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 while the bus is idle and externally released. Allow the WRITE command to enter its SDA-setting phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=0 side of the specified behavior: during the SDA-setting phase of each WRITE bit, before or while SCL is released for the high phase, sda_oen is 0, driving SDA low.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, monitor in_write_sequence and identify the SDA-setting phase from the WRITE timing/output sequence; compare sda_oen against 0 whenever din=0, and verify the driven bus SDA is low when no external participant overrides it.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and a supported clk_cnt, then issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 while the bus is idle and externally released. Allow the WRITE command to enter its SDA-setting phase and released high phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=1 side of the specified behavior: during the SDA-setting phase of each WRITE bit, before or while SCL is released for the high phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, monitor in_write_sequence and identify the SDA-setting phase from the WRITE timing/output sequence; compare sda_oen against 1 whenever din=1, and verify the released bus SDA is high when no external participant drives it low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), and drive din=1 with the external SDA and SCL lines released high. Hold these conditions and provide enabled clock edges until the WRITE sequence completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of observed_via.shows: during the WRITE stable-high phase scl_oen is 1, then scl_oen becomes 0 to pull SCL low again; the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at the terminal WRITE phase.
elements.check_method: Use the in_write_sequence and in_idle probes to identify the WRITE window and completion. At settled posedge observations, assert that scl_oen has a 1-to-0 transition after the stable high phase, that in_idle becomes 1, and that cmd_ack is high for one cycle followed by low. Fail if the release-then-pull-low sequence or acknowledgement is absent.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), and drive din=1. During the WRITE stable-high phase after scl_oen releases SCL, externally pull SDA low to cause arbitration loss, and hold it low through the next enabled clock.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of observed_via.shows: the normal required scl_oen release-then-pull-low completion behavior and one-clock cmd_ack do not occur. Instead, arbitration loss aborts the WRITE, al asserts, the FSM returns to idle, both output enables are released, and cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Detect the stable-high phase using in_write_sequence and sda_arbitration_check, then verify al asserts after filtered SDA is low while din=1. Check that no cmd_ack pulse occurs for this command, that in_idle becomes 1, and that scl_oen and sda_oen are both 1 after abort rather than observing the normal completion sequence.

elements.stimulus: With ena high and a released-high bus, issue START, STOP, WRITE with din=0, and READ commands sequentially. During every observed command phase, monitor scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen.
elements.expected_response: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout idle and all START, STOP, WRITE, and READ phases. Whenever a line is actively pulled low, its corresponding output enable is 0; whenever the line is released, its output enable is 1. No output enable state causes a high drive.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-by-cycle assertion and scoreboard keyed to the command FSM phase: assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 always, and verify the observed bus line equals low when its enable is 0 and otherwise is not driven by the DUT.

elements.stimulus: Exercise WRITE with din=0 and din=1, and READ with external SDA returning 0 and 1. Include the phases where SDA is actively driven low and where SDA is released, and include SCL low-drive and released-high phases.
elements.expected_response: For WRITE din=0, SDA is actively pulled low using sda_oen=0; for WRITE din=1 and READ, SDA is released using sda_oen=1 during the data high/read window. SCL uses scl_oen=0 only for low phases and scl_oen=1 for released phases. scl_o and sda_o remain 0 for all data values and phases.
elements.check_method: Compare each phase against an open-drain bus model: DUT drive contribution is low when the corresponding enable is 0 and high-impedance when it is 1; assert that no DUT output can source a high level, regardless of din or external SDA value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a valid START command with ena high and clk_cnt configured to allow progress. Model the external bus as released high and sample the phase in which the START sequence actively pulls SDA low; also observe any phase in which SCL is actively pulled low.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0143: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout. During each active-low line phase, the corresponding output enable is 0: sda_oen is 0 when SDA is actively pulled low and scl_oen is 0 when SCL is actively pulled low. The driven bus line is consequently low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge sample, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. Use the START-sequence probe and output-enable transition trace to compare each active phase against the expected enable polarity, and compare the modeled open-drain bus level with the corresponding enable.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus externally released high, leave the controller idle long enough to observe its released state, then issue a valid START followed by a valid STOP with ena high. Capture the START phase before SDA is pulled low and the STOP phase after SCL is released and while SDA is released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of REQ-0143: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 throughout. During released-line phases, the corresponding output enable is 1: scl_oen is 1 when SCL is released and sda_oen is 1 when SDA is released. With no external low drive, the modeled bus lines are high during those release phases.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge sample, assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0. Check the idle, START, and STOP phase probes against scl_oen==1 or sda_oen==1 for each released line, and verify the open-drain bus model resolves each released line high when the external participant does not pull it low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and wait until the START sequence reaches its SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: sda_oen is 0 and sda_o is 0, so SDA is driven low. The corresponding SCL outputs remain in the released phase with scl_oen=1 and scl_o=0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, use the START-sequence probe or observed output phase to identify the SDA-low phase; assert sda_oen==0 and sda_o==0, and compare the effective open-drain line value against the expected driven-low value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and sample the initial START-sequence release phase before SDA is pulled low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sda_oen is 1, indicating SDA is released rather than driven by this controller; sda_o remains 0 as the constant open-drain output. The SDA line therefore remains high when no external device pulls it low.
elements.check_method: During the initial START release phase, assert sda_oen==1 and sda_o==0, and with the external SDA driver released verify the modeled wired-AND SDA line is high; ensure this differs from the sda_oen==0 drive case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and wait until the START sequence advances to the phase that pulls SCL low after SDA has been asserted low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen is 0 and scl_o is 0, so SCL is driven low. The corresponding SDA output remains asserted for the START condition with sda_oen=0 and sda_o=0.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, identify the SCL-low START phase using the START-sequence probe and output history; assert scl_oen==0 and scl_o==0, and compare the effective wired-AND SCL line value with driven-low.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, issue cmd=START, and sample the initial START phase while SCL is released before the sequence pulls it low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen is 1, indicating SCL is released rather than driven by this controller; scl_o remains 0 as the constant open-drain output. With no external SCL pull-low, the modeled SCL line remains high.
elements.check_method: During the initial SCL release phase, assert scl_oen==1 and scl_o==0, and with the external SCL driver released verify the modeled wired-AND SCL line is high; ensure this differs from the scl_oen==0 drive case.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep external SCL and SDA undriven so the pull-ups make them high, then issue a START command and observe the initial START phase while the controller has released SCL.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen: scl_oen is high, indicating that SCL is released and the external pull-up can bring the SCL line high; the modeled SCL line is high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the release phase, compare scl_oen against 1 and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SCL high when no external device drives it low.

elements.stimulus: With the controller executing a START command, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 and allow the START sequence to advance from its released-SCL phase to the phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for scl_oen: scl_oen is low, indicating that SCL is actively pulled low rather than released; the modeled SCL line is low even with the external pull-up present.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge for the low-drive phase, compare scl_oen against 0 and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SCL low.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, leave the external bus undriven, then issue a START command and observe the initial START phase before SDA is driven low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for sda_oen: sda_oen is high, indicating that SDA is released and the external pull-up can bring the SDA line high; the modeled SDA line is high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the released-SDA phase, compare sda_oen against 1 and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SDA high when no external device drives it low.

elements.stimulus: With the controller executing a START command, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 and allow the sequence to reach the START condition in which SDA is pulled low while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for sda_oen: sda_oen is low, indicating that SDA is actively pulled low rather than released; the modeled SDA line is low despite the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At the settled posedge for the START-condition phase, compare sda_oen against 0 and verify the open-drain bus model resolves SDA low.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1 and cmd=START, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and drive clk until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase and returns toward idle.
elements.expected_response: The START output-enable sequence completes, then cmd_ack is high for exactly the one clk cycle corresponding to sequence completion; cmd_ack is low on the immediately preceding and following clk cycles. This is the holding case of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the in_start_sequence and in_idle probes to identify sequence entry and completion, sample cmd_ack after each posedge clk, and assert a one-cycle pulse exactly at completion with no adjacent high cycles.

elements.stimulus: After establishing a busy transaction, set ena=1 and cmd=STOP, keep the external SCL line able to rise when released, and drive clk until the STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The STOP output-enable sequence completes, then cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle at sequence completion and low before and after that cycle. This is the holding case of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Track in_stop_sequence and the terminal transition to in_idle; compare the registered cmd_ack waveform against a reference pulse located at the completion edge and assert that its width is one clk cycle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, set din=0, issue cmd=WRITE, provide a released-high SCL response with SDA low as appropriate for the written zero, and drive clk until the WRITE sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE output-enable sequence completes without abort, then cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle at sequence completion and low on all other sampled cycles. This is the holding case of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use in_write_sequence and the sequence terminal transition to define completion, then assert cmd_ack has one and only one high sample at that point and remains low for the next cycle.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set ena=1, issue cmd=READ, release SDA and provide external SCL rising and falling phases, then drive clk until the READ sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: The READ output-enable and sampling sequence completes, then cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle at sequence completion and low before and after that cycle. This is the holding case of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use in_read_sequence and the terminal phase/return to idle to identify completion; compare cmd_ack to a reference one-clock pulse and flag any missing, early, late, or multi-cycle assertion.

elements.stimulus: Issue each recognized command in separate trials with ena=1, then sample cmd_ack on every clk throughout the active sequence, including all non-terminal phases and the cycles immediately before and after completion; also issue NOP while idle as a control trial.
elements.expected_response: When the requirement does not hold—before terminal completion, after the one completion cycle, or for NOP—cmd_ack is absent (low). For each recognized command, any assertion that is mistimed relative to terminal completion or remains high for more than one clk cycle is a failure of the required behavior. This is the contrasting case of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model keyed to the command-sequence terminal event and assert cmd_ack=0 on every non-completion cycle, cmd_ack=1 on exactly the completion cycle, and cmd_ack=0 on the following cycle; separately assert no pulse for NOP.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command, and observe the sequence before its terminal phase is reached.
elements.expected_response: This is the not-completed side of the requirement's observed_via shows clause: cmd_ack remains low on every clock while the START sequence is still in progress.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while in_start_sequence is active and before the terminal phase, assert cmd_ack==0 using a clocked monitor.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command on a released-high bus, and run until the START sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the completed side of the requirement's observed_via shows clause: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle when the START operation completes, then returns low so the next bit command can be issued.
elements.check_method: Monitor the START terminal transition and require cmd_ack==1 on exactly the corresponding registered completion cycle, with cmd_ack==0 on the preceding and following clocks; count exactly one high cycle.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction with START, then set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a STOP command, and provide released-high SCL so the STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the completed side of the requirement's observed_via shows clause: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle at STOP completion and returns low thereafter.
elements.check_method: Use the stop-sequence terminal-state probe and a clocked assertion that cmd_ack is high for one and only one settled posedge at completion, low before completion, and low on the next clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command, release SDA, allow SCL to rise normally, and run through the complete read bit cycle.
elements.expected_response: This is the completed side of the requirement's observed_via shows clause: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle after the READ operation reaches completion, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Detect the READ terminal phase with in_read_sequence and verify a single cmd_ack high cycle associated with completion, with no cmd_ack high during the active read phases or on the following clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command with din=0, provide a normal released-high SCL phase without arbitration loss, and run through the complete write bit cycle.
elements.expected_response: This is the completed side of the requirement's observed_via shows clause: cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle when the WRITE operation completes and returns low afterward.
elements.check_method: Detect the WRITE terminal phase with in_write_sequence and check that cmd_ack is high on exactly one registered cycle at completion, low before completion, and low on the immediately subsequent cycle.
